artigo.texto: O Rio Grande do Norte tem nove projetos de parques de baterias com processos de licenciamento ambiental abertos, segundo o Instituto de Desenvolvimento Sustentável e Meio Ambiente (Idema). Os empreendimentos estão em fase inicial, com os Termos de Referência já emitidos e os responsáveis dentro do prazo para apresentar os estudos ambientais necessários à análise dos pedidos. A maioria dos projetos está associada a parques eólicos e usinas solares, em um movimento que pode ampliar as possibilidades de aproveitamento da energia renovável produzida no estado. O armazenamento por baterias ganha relevância diante das restrições à geração de eletricidade e das limitações da rede de transmissão para absorver toda a energia disponível. >> Faça parte do canal do Movimento Econômico no WhatsApp Entre os maiores empreendimentos em análise, está um projeto da empresa SCATEC Renováveis, em Assú, no Vale do Açu, classificado como excepcional e com capacidade informada de 1.920 MW/h de armazenamento. Também estão na lista um projeto de 1.440 MW em João Câmara e outro de 1.200 MW/h em Mossoró. Este último, segundo o Idema, não está vinculado a um empreendimento de energia renovável. De acordo com Werner Farkatt, diretor-geral do Idema, há outros empreendedores que já procuraram o órgão para discutir projetos, mas ainda não formalizaram os pedidos. Por isso, o número oficial permanece em nove processos. Baterias podem aproveitar energia que não chega à rede A instalação desses sistemas está relacionada a um dos desafios do setor elétrico: a dificuldade de escoar toda a energia gerada em determinados períodos. Quando a produção supera a capacidade de transmissão ou a demanda, pode ser necessário reduzir a geração de parques eólicos e solares. As baterias permitem armazenar parte dessa eletricidade para disponibilizá-la posteriormente, em momentos de maior consumo ou quando a geração diminui. A tecnologia também pode contribuir para integrar diferentes fontes renováveis, inclusive em empreendimentos que combinam geração eólica e solar, conhecidos como parques híbridos. “Com as baterias ou data centers ou hidrogênios, essa energia que em teoria seria canalizada para rede nacional, para as nossas casas, nossas indústrias, seriam revertidas para esses equipamentos”, afirma Farkatt. Segundo o diretor-geral, a expansão dessas estruturas também pode estimular a atividade econômica nos municípios que recebem os empreendimentos. Diferentemente de parte dos parques de geração, cuja demanda por trabalhadores diminui depois da construção, os novos equipamentos podem exigir equipes permanentes para operação e manutenção. “Esses outros equipamentos precisam de mão de obra full-time. Então, isso vai envolver novamente um aquecimento do mercado de trabalho”, acrescenta. O impacto potencial alcança ainda fornecedores, prestadores de serviços, comércio e mercado imobiliário, com reflexos na demanda por hospedagem, alimentação, combustíveis e manutenção de veículos e equipamentos. Regras específicas dão previsibilidade aos investimentos Em 2026, o Rio Grande do Norte aprovou, no Conselho Estadual de Meio Ambiente, três resoluções para disciplinar o licenciamento ambiental de projetos de hidrogênio, sistemas de armazenamento por baterias e data centers. As normas foram elaboradas por grupos técnicos com participação de profissionais do Idema e de outras instituições, incluindo órgãos estaduais e representantes do setor produtivo. A proposta é estabelecer previamente os procedimentos e os estudos exigidos conforme o porte e o potencial de impacto de cada empreendimento. Os Termos de Referência orientam os empreendedores sobre a documentação necessária para solicitar as licenças. “Isso traz não só a questão da segurança jurídica, porque não foi um ato normativo criado por uma portaria ou um ato administrativo. Ele passou por uma função ampla no conselho e teve aprovação do corpo colegiado. Isso traz uma legalidade mais robusta ao ato do licenciamento”, afirma Farkatt. No caso das baterias, os projetos seguem as exigências correspondentes às suas características. Estruturas com capacidade inferior a 10 MW/h de armazenamento, conforme informado pelo diretor, são dispensadas de licença ambiental e recebem uma declaração formal de dispensa. Apesar do avanço regulatório, os nove processos ainda dependem da apresentação dos estudos ambientais pelos empreendedores para que o instituto possa dar continuidade à análise. Hidrogênio verde e data centers ampliam a agenda Além das baterias, o estado já registra movimentação no licenciamento de projetos de hidrogênio. Um empreendimento em Areia Branca, o complexo Morro Pintado, da Brasil Green Energy, recebeu licença prévia e protocolou, em 10 de outubro, o pedido de licença de instalação, que está em análise, segundo o Idema. O projeto foi associado a investimentos estimados em R$ 12 bilhões e à produção de hidrogênio verde. Outro empreendimento de hidrogênio, na região de São Gonçalo do Amarante, na Grande Natal, já recebeu licença de instalação. A proposta prevê o uso de energia renovável e água de reúso proveniente do tratamento de esgoto do município. Para os data centers, entretanto, o Idema ainda não recebeu pedidos formais de licenciamento. Segundo Farkatt, empresas já haviam procurado o órgão para obter informações sobre as regras, antes da aprovação da resolução específica. A expectativa é que, com os critérios definidos, os interessados avancem na avaliação da viabilidade de seus projetos. artigo.texto: Jaipur Discom and GEAPP Launch Sodium-Ion Battery Pilot 02 Nov 2026 2 Min Read CW Team Share Jaipur Discom and global not-for-profit organisation GEAPP have launched a pilot project to assess sodium-ion battery storage for renewable power at the distribution transformer level in Jaipur. The initiative aims to help manage peak electricity demand and improve the use of energy generated by rooftop solar installations in Rajasthan. The entities have invited industry proposals to develop a 250 kilowatt-hour (kWh) battery energy storage system at KL Saini Stadium in the Mansarovar area of Jaipur. The request for proposal was issued during the second day of a national conference of electricity distribution companies being held in the city. The project will examine whether storing electricity closer to consumers can help maintain supply during periods of high demand and reduce pressure on local transformers. It will also assess sodium-ion batteries as an alternative to lithium-ion technology, including their performance under Rajasthan’s climatic conditions. Jaipur Discom will provide the project site, technical personnel and operational data. GEAPP will support system design, performance monitoring and technical work, while also training engineers from the distribution company. The pilot is intended to generate operational evidence from a working electricity network rather than relying solely on estimates. Rajasthan Energy Secretary and Discoms Chairperson Arti Dogra said the impact of rising demand during peak hours was first experienced at the distribution transformer level. She said the project would assess the ability of battery storage to ease transformer loads, store rooftop solar power and improve distribution network performance. GEAPP India Country Head Tanya Singhal said energy storage would become increasingly important to India’s electricity grid and that distribution companies needed dependable technology options beyond lithium-ion batteries. The organisations will share the pilot’s findings with electricity distribution companies across the country to support future decisions on energy storage systems. artigo.texto: Tamil Nadu Approves 100 Per Cent Charge Waiver for BESS 02 Nov 2026 2 Min Read CW Team Share The Tamil Nadu state cabinet has approved the Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Policy 2026 after detailed discussions, with the policy aimed at accelerating the installation of battery storage across power generation and transmission networks. It covers projects with a capacity of 1 MW and above and seeks to improve renewable energy utilisation while reducing the curtailment of electricity generated from renewable sources. The policy recognises two categories of battery storage systems: standalone BESS and co-located BESS. Standalone BESS refers to independent systems with a capacity of more than 1 MW, which can be connected to transmission or distribution networks or to private consumer networks. Standalone projects will be eligible for a 100 per cent waiver of applicable transmission and wheeling charges. The systems can be used to meet peak-hour demand, support grid operations and provide other services approved under the policy. Co-located BESS refers to storage systems integrated with solar, solar-hybrid or other renewable energy projects with a capacity of more than 1 MW. These systems will store electricity produced by associated renewable energy plants and supply it during peak-demand periods or whenever required. Co-located BESS projects linked to existing or new solar, wind or hybrid projects will also receive a 100 per cent waiver of applicable transmission and wheeling charges. The policy will apply to all BESS projects for which applications are submitted on or after the date of notification, as well as projects commissioned on or after April 1, 2027. By covering both independent storage installations and systems paired with renewable energy projects, the policy establishes a common framework for deploying BESS across the state’s electricity network. The incentives are intended to support storage use during periods of peak demand and help renewable power reach the grid when it is needed. artigo.texto: For a long time, an inverter had one primary job: keep essential appliances running when the power went out. Customers typically looked at three things when choosing one: how much load it could handle, how long the backup would last and how reliably it performed. That is beginning to change. As India expands its renewable energy capacity and adopts energy storage across more applications, the role of the inverter is evolving. It is no longer simply a backup device. It is becoming an important part of how electricity is converted, managed and delivered across homes, businesses and larger power systems. This shift has implications for the entire energy storage industry. The focus can no longer be on how much energy a battery can store alone. We also need to consider how efficiently that energy is converted, when it is used and how reliably the system performs under real-world conditions. India’s energy transition is changing the role of the inverter India’s growing renewable energy capacity brings an important challenge. Solar power generation depends on sunlight, while electricity demand follows its own pattern. The hours when solar generation is highest do not always coincide with the hours when electricity is needed most. Energy storage can help bridge this gap. It allows electricity to be stored when it is available and used when demand rises or generation falls. Beyond backup, storage can support peak-demand management, improve the utilisation of renewable energy and add flexibility to the power system. The scale of the opportunity is significant. According to the Central Electricity Authority’s National Electricity Plan, India’s projected energy storage requirement is 411.4 GWh by 2031–32, including 236.22 GWh of battery energy storage. These are projected requirements rather than installed capacity, but they give us a sense of the infrastructure India may need in the coming years. For the power electronics industry, this changes the conversation. The challenge is no longer limited to converting the direct current stored in a battery into alternating current for everyday use. Systems must also manage changing loads, operate efficiently and respond reliably to different electrical conditions. A battery is only as useful as the system around it Much of the discussion around energy storage focuses on battery chemistry, capacity, cycle life and charging performance. These are important considerations, but they tell only part of the story. The inverter, battery management system, control logic and protection mechanisms all influence how effectively stored energy is used. If these components are not designed to work together, the system may not deliver the performance a customer expects, even if the battery itself is capable. Consider a commercial facility that generates solar power during the day but experiences higher electricity demand in the evening. The value of its storage system depends on more than the amount of energy stored. It also depends on how efficiently the system charges and discharges, manages changing loads and minimises conversion losses. The same principle applies to homes, shops, offices and industrial facilities, although each application has different requirements. This is why we need to evaluate an inverter as part of an integrated energy storage system, rather than as an independent product. The shift from backup power to smarter energy management Customers are becoming more interested in how an energy storage system performs in everyday use, not simply how long it can provide backup during an outage. Can it handle changes in load? Is it compatible with the intended battery configuration? How does it respond to fluctuations in the electricity supply? Can its performance be monitored? What happens when operating temperatures or energy requirements change? These are practical questions, and the answers will increasingly influence buying decisions. I believe system integration will become one of the strongest differentiators in this market. The inverter, battery, controls and protection systems must work together as a reliable unit. Monitoring and diagnostic features can add value by helping users understand performance, identify potential issues and make informed maintenance decisions. However, adding software or connectivity does not automatically make a product better. Digital features are useful only when they are supported by sound engineering, reliable hardware and meaningful performance data. The objective should be straightforward: make energy systems more reliable, efficient and easier to manage. Grid-forming inverters and the next stage of grid stability One of the important developments in power electronics is the growing attention being paid to grid-forming inverter technology. As renewable energy and battery storage account for a larger share of electricity systems, maintaining stable grid voltage and frequency becomes an increasingly important engineering challenge. Grid-forming inverters are designed to establish and support aspects of grid behaviour, depending on their capabilities and the conditions in which they operate. India’s regulatory and technical discussions are also moving in this direction. Developments involving the Central Electricity Authority and proposed grid-connectivity requirements for renewable energy and storage projects reflect the growing importance of inverter capabilities in future power systems. The specific requirements, however, depend on the applicable regulations and the nature of each project. This is an important distinction. Adding more generation and storage capacity is necessary, but the electricity system must also be able to manage that capacity reliably. Grid-forming technology is particularly relevant to larger grid-connected applications. A residential inverter does not necessarily need the same capabilities as a utility-scale system. The AI boom is creating a new reality for electric utilities. Utilities will soon need to support gigawatt-scale data center developments while continuing to deliver reliable, affordable power to their existing residential, commercial, and industrial customers. artigo.texto: Empresas investem mais em data centers, mas traduzir os dados em eficiência operacional é desafio para 2027 Investimentos globais em data centers podem alcançar US$ 3 trilhões em 5 anos O avanço da Inteligência Artificial tem estabelecido uma corrida global por infraestrutura digital. No Brasil, esse movimento ganhou força nos últimos meses, impulsionado pelo avanço de projetos de infraestrutura para data centers e pela crescente demanda por processamento de dados, aplicações de IA generativa, computação em nuvem e serviços digitais. Segundo estimativas da Moody’s, os investimentos globais em data centers podem alcançar cerca de US$ 3 trilhões nos próximos cinco anos. O cenário também se reflete no Brasil. Segundo o Ministério de Minas e Energia, o país soma 38 GW em pedidos de acesso à rede elétrica para novos projetos de data centers. Desse total, 7,1 GW correspondem a empreendimentos já mapeados, com potencial de movimentar cerca de R$ 159 bilhões em investimentos nos próximos anos. O movimento reforça o posicionamento do Brasil como um dos principais mercados para a expansão da infraestrutura digital na América Latina e amplia as perspectivas para o avanço da Inteligência Artificial no ambiente corporativo. O aumento da capacidade computacional cria as condições para acelerar a adoção da Inteligência Artificial, mas também evidencia um desafio enfrentado por muitas organizações: transformar essa infraestrutura em resultados concretos para o negócio. Sem uma base de dados estruturada, integração entre sistemas e governança da informação, o potencial da IA pode ser limitado, mesmo em ambientes com alta capacidade de processamento. Para a Engineering Brasil, companhia global especializada em transformação digital, IA, APIs e dados, parte do Grupo Engineering, o fortalecimento da infraestrutura representa um passo importante para acelerar a adoção da tecnologia nas empresas. No entanto, a organização alerta que a capacidade computacional, por si só, não garante ganhos de produtividade, inovação ou retorno sobre os investimentos. Segundo Fabricio Pellizon, gerente executivo de Arquitetura e Implementação de Nuvem da Engineering Brasil, existe o risco de o mercado concentrar seus esforços apenas na expansão da infraestrutura, deixando em segundo plano desafios fundamentais relacionados à qualidade dos dados, à integração dos sistemas e à maturidade das arquiteturas corporativas. “Os investimentos em data centers são essenciais para sustentar o crescimento da Inteligência Artificial, mas representam apenas a camada visível dessa transformação. A capacidade de processamento precisa estar conectada a uma base sólida de dados, governança e integração. Sem isso, as empresas podem ampliar sua infraestrutura tecnológica sem conseguir converter esse investimento em eficiência operacional, inovação ou geração de valor para o negócio“, afirma. O desafio está na base tecnológica das empresas Embora a disponibilidade de infraestrutura seja um pré-requisito para o avanço da IA, muitas organizações ainda enfrentam obstáculos relacionados à integração de sistemas, governança de dados, interoperabilidade entre plataformas e modernização de ambientes legados. Na prática, mesmo empresas com acesso às tecnologias mais avançadas podem encontrar dificuldades para escalar projetos de IA ou capturar benefícios consistentes. Segundo análise da McKinsey publicada em junho de 2026, mais de dois terços das empresas de alta performance apontam os dados como o principal obstáculo para viabilizar a IA. O levantamento mostra ainda que apenas 7% das organizações conseguiram escalar completamente a tecnologia em toda a empresa. Nesse cenário, dados dispersos, informações inconsistentes e ambientes fragmentados tornam-se barreiras para construir aplicações confiáveis e ampliar o uso da tecnologia. Segundo Pellizon, a corrida pela Inteligência Artificial está criando uma prioridade para as organizações: preparar a base tecnológica que sustentará as aplicações dos próximos anos. “A discussão sobre IA costuma se concentrar nos modelos, na infraestrutura e no poder computacional. Mas o que realmente determina o sucesso dessas iniciativas é a capacidade de conectar dados, sistemas e processos de negócio. Quanto mais sofisticadas se tornam as aplicações, maior é a necessidade de uma arquitetura preparada para operar com escala, confiabilidade e governança”, explica. A Engineering Brasil, que apoia empresas dos setores de telecomunicações, energia, indústria e serviços na construção de ambientes capazes de transformar dados em ativos estratégicos e criar as condições necessárias para o uso sustentável da Inteligência Artificial, vem ampliando sua atuação em projetos voltados à modernização de arquiteturas corporativas, integração de dados, plataformas digitais e governança da informação. Para o executivo, o diferencial competitivo dos próximos anos não estará apenas no acesso à infraestrutura ou aos modelos mais avançados, mas na capacidade de transformar dados em decisões mais rápidas, processos mais eficientes e novas oportunidades de negócio. “O verdadeiro retorno sobre os investimentos em IA não será definido pela quantidade de servidores instalados ou pela capacidade computacional disponível. O que vai diferenciar as empresas será a qualidade da arquitetura que conecta dados, aplicações e operações. A infraestrutura abre caminho, mas o valor real surge quando a tecnologia consegue transformar informação em inteligência e inteligência em resultado”, conclui. Crédito da imagem- Magnific

artigo.texto: Mecpower Solutions, Navitas Solar Plan 5 GWh BESS Facility 02 Nov 2026 2 Min Read CW Team Share Mecpower Solutions and Navitas Solar have collaborated to establish a 5 GWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) manufacturing facility in Karjan, Gujarat. The proposed facility is expected to begin operations in the first quarter of FY2027-28, according to an announcement by Navitas Solar. The companies said the project would support rising demand for integrated energy storage solutions across India’s renewable energy sector. The collaboration combines Mecpower Solutions’ capabilities in renewable energy project development, engineering and execution with Navitas Solar’s integrated manufacturing expertise. The proposed facility is intended to bring together manufacturing, project deployment and system integration capabilities. The companies plan to develop scalable storage solutions for utility-scale, commercial and industrial renewable energy applications, while supporting their respective engineering, procurement and construction deployments and utility-scale projects. BESS facilities are becoming an important part of renewable energy infrastructure because they can help manage the intermittency of solar and wind generation, improve grid stability and enable more efficient use of renewable power. The companies said the collaboration would strengthen domestic energy storage capabilities in line with India’s long-term renewable energy objectives. Setul Shah, director of Mecpower Solutions, said the facility would strengthen the company’s position across the energy storage value chain by combining manufacturing with its engineering, procurement and construction and independent power producer businesses. He said the project was intended to support the development of more flexible and reliable renewable power systems. Ankit Singhania, director of Navitas Solar, said domestic manufacturing would help strengthen India’s clean-energy supply chain and address the requirements of utility-scale storage projects. He added that the partnership would extend Navitas Solar’s manufacturing capabilities into energy storage and contribute to scalable solutions for India’s power sector. artigo.texto: Rodan Energy Solutions Inc. and St. Marys Cement Inc., a subsidiary of Votorantim Cimentos North America (VCNA), announced a long-term agreement for the development, ownership, and optimisation of a 50 MWh behind-the-meter battery energy storage system (BESS) at St. Marys Cement’s Bowmanville, Ontario facility – becoming Canada’s largest behind-the-meter BESS installation to date. For St. Marys Cement and VCNA, the project represents an important step in VCNA’s broader strategy to improve energy performance, operational resilience, and sustainability. The plant has operated in Bowmanville since 1968, and VCNA has continued to invest in the facility and the surrounding community. The battery system will allow the plant to reduce its grid demand during periods of peak electricity use, while maintaining essential operations. It will also enable the batteries to be charged during lower-demand periods and used during high peak demand periods. This reduces demand on the grid when electricity carbon intensity can be higher. The project supports VCNA’s sustainability roadmap, including its commitment to net-zero concrete by 2050 and interim 2030 targets. Rodan Energy will develop, own, and operate the asset, delivering ongoing energy optimisation through its proprietary FlexOps platform. The project will deliver significant economic value by providing grid flexibility resources and energy cost savings, support VCNA’s sustainability goals, and strengthen the operational resiliency of the Bowmanville plant. Rodan assumes the development capital and operational risk; St. Marys Cement benefits from a fully managed, long-term energy solution with no upfront capital outlay. “This agreement is a demonstration of what behind-the-meter BESS can deliver for large industrial energy users – real economic savings, a lower emissions footprint, and energy security they control. Rodan owns and operates the asset, so our performance is tied directly to delivering meaningful outcomes for our client. We are actively building a North American portfolio of projects like this one, and we are looking for the right C&I partners, financiers, battery manufacturers, and EPCs to grow with us.” Said Paul Grod, President and CEO of Rodan Energy Solutions “Our Bowmanville plant has been part of the community since 1968, and we have continued to invest in its long-term performance. This project brings together energy cost management, operational resilience and our sustainability roadmap in a practical way. By helping us reduce demand on the grid during periods of peak system demand while supporting reliable plant operations, the project reflects Sustainable Legacy, one of the values of Our VC Way, and our commitment to creating lasting value for our operations and communities. Rodan brings the technical capability, long-term commitment and operational depth to help us deliver these outcomes over the life of the asset.” Said Jorge Wagner, President and CEO of Votorantim Cimentos North America As VCNA’s first project of this type, the Bowmanville installation creates a foundation for evaluating similar opportunities across other VCNA operations. It demonstrates how targeted energy infrastructure can support reliable production, cost efficiency and progress toward the company’s sustainability commitments. The St. Marys project runs on Rodan’s FlexOps optimisation platform, which currently manages over 1,500 MW of distributed energy resources – including curtail-able load, generation, and grid-connected and behind-the-meter battery storage systems – across North America. The portfolio is rapidly scaling to meet the significant North American electricity market demand. Rodan is actively expanding its behind-the-meter BESS portfolio and invites partnerships from C&I energy users seeking long-term energy cost and resiliency solutions, as well as battery manufacturers, EPCs, investors, and financial institutions interested in participating in that growth. The company is also in active discussions with hyperscalers, large-footprint data centre operators, industrial and commercial consumers, electric vehicle fleets and utilities (for whom behind-the-meter storage is an increasingly practical solution to power demand), grid constraints, and clean energy commitments.

artigo.texto: Gasgoo Munich- Gotion High-Tech (002074.SZ) released its third-quarter report for 2026 on the evening of Oct. 28. Revenue for the first three quarters hit 45.437 billion yuan, a 53.98% jump from a year earlier, while net profit excluding non-recurring items surged 195.54% to 252 million yuan. On the business front, Gotion's growing market share in power batteries shored up its earnings base. Its energy storage operations are shifting from simple supply and delivery to general engineering contracting, opening new market space. The partnership with Volkswagen now extends to co-building overseas capacity, offering fresh supply-chain support for its global push. Image Source: Gotion High-Tech Data from the China Automotive Power Battery Innovation Alliance shows domestic power battery installations reached 576.3 GWh in the first three quarters, up 16.7% year-on-year. Gotion's installations hit 34.89 GWh during the same period — a 32.81% gain that lifted its market share to 6.07%, up 0.74 percentage points from a year earlier. Globally, SNE Research data puts the company's installations at 41.5 GWh from January through August, climbing 47.1% — well ahead of the 19.7% global market growth rate. That keeps Gotion ranked fifth worldwide. In passenger vehicles, Gotion is deepening ties with major automakers including Chery, Geely, and Leapmotor. It supplies LFP batteries for the entire Chery QQ3EV lineup, a model that has topped 10,000 in monthly sales for six straight months. Gotion also remains Leapmotor's top cell supplier, powering core models like the A10, B10, C11, and C16, and ranks as the primary provider across several of those vehicles. Beyond passenger cars, new-energy heavy trucks are emerging as a key growth frontier for the company's battery business. Industry figures show Gotion's heavy-truck battery installations ranked among the top five from January to August, jumping 51.5% year-on-year. The main hurdle for electrifying heavy trucks is transport economics. Tackling that pain point, Gotion has kept pushing product upgrades. On Oct. 20, it rolled out a new-generation CTB rear-integrated heavy-truck battery. Compared with traditional single-pack setups, the system sheds roughly 400 kg from the vehicle and covers battery capacities from 400 to 700 kWh. Meanwhile, Gotion's partnership with Volkswagen is pushing its global footprint into deeper territory. The two sides already cooperate on equity, standard cell development, and large-scale supply. Gotion's first-half report shows it sold roughly 2.536 billion yuan worth of materials and cells to Volkswagen (China) and affiliates in the first half of 2026, laying a business foundation for deeper supply-chain ties. In September, Gotion detailed plans to step up its partnership with the Volkswagen Group. The two intend to set up three joint ventures in Spain, Slovakia, and Morocco, building lithium battery plants with annual capacities of 29.1 GWh and 8.4 GWh, respectively, plus an LFP cathode material facility producing 100,000 tons a year. A wholly-owned Gotion subsidiary is also slated to handle engineering for the Valencia battery project in Spain. Unlike past moves that simply planted overseas capacity, this collaboration links the entire chain — from upstream materials and cell manufacturing to local supply for downstream customers.

artigo.texto: RatedPower, a leading provider of software for solar plant design and optimization, is organizing a free webinar on November 18 to explain how grid constraints, permitting, and land availability influence co-located solar and battery project design, and how investors and developers can use its software to make better decisions and avoid issues such as financing delays, increased costs, and reduced returns. The webinar, titled “Financial viability of co-located PV + BESS projects: a Balkans case study,” will feature a speaker from GMS Consult, a Serbian client of RatedPower. Grid constraints, permitting, and land availability often surface late in a co-located solar and battery energy storage system (BESS) project, when changing the layout is expensive. They can reshape the business case, delay financing, or cut returns, RatedPower explains in the webinar announcement. At the online event on November 18, Vladimir Antušević, Senior Electrical Engineer at Serbia-based renewable energy design and consulting firm GMS Consult, will share his experience with RatedPower software in his day-to-day work, including how quickly design changes can be evaluated. According to Antušević, RatedPower helps engineers and developers make key technical and economic decisions from the very beginning. GMS Consult’s Vladimir Antušević will share his experience with RatedPower software in day-to-day work RatedPower’s Emil Trepin and Matteo Menazzi, for their part, will demonstrate how different PV + BESS configurations affect performance, costs, and financial viability, using RatedPower and the Power Analyst platform. By bringing both perspectives together, the webinar will offer attendees the opportunity to learn how to assess the influence of grid constraints, permitting, and land availability on PV + BESS project design; explore different co-located PV and BESS configurations and their impact on project viability; connect technical design decisions with financial analysis; evaluate project performance and costs using RatedPower and Power Analyst; and make more informed decisions throughout the project development process. It is vital to understand the constraints early in the project development process “The earlier you understand how grid, land, and permitting constraints affect a project, the better positioned you are to protect its financial viability,” says Emil Trepin, Account Executive at RatedPower. Matteo Menazzi, Technical Advisor at RatedPower, explains that comparing PV and BESS configurations early helps teams understand how design decisions translate into performance, costs, and overall project viability. Registrations for the webinar are now open, and those who cannot attend live will receive a recording of the event, according to the announcement. RatedPower is part of Enverus, a global software-as-a-service (SaaS) platform for the energy sector. It offers a one-stop cloud-based solution for PV plant and BESS design and engineering, as well as hybrid systems.

artigo.texto: VinEnergo has commissioned a rooftop solar power system integrated with a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) in the Vung Ang Economic Zone in Ha Tinh, Vietnam. The project will supply clean electricity to the VinFast electric vehicle manufacturing plant, the VinES battery manufacturing facility and the VG battery manufacturing joint venture. The project marks VinEnergo’s first operational renewable energy installation under the Direct Power Purchase Agreement (DPPA) mechanism. It is designed to support the electricity requirements of major industrial facilities while reducing dependence on conventional grid power. The initial beneficiaries include Future Production, Investment and Development Joint Stock Company, which owns and operates the VinFast electric car and motorcycle manufacturing plant in Ha Tinh, and VinES Ha Tinh Energy Solutions Joint Stock Company, the operator of the VinES battery manufacturing facility. The rooftop solar installation will also supply electricity to the VG joint venture battery factory within the same electric vehicle and battery manufacturing complex. According to company estimates, the integrated solar and storage system is expected to generate approximately 39 million kWh of clean electricity during its first year of operation. The project is projected to reduce carbon dioxide emissions by more than 25,000 tonnes annually, equivalent to the estimated annual carbon absorption of over 1.13 million trees. The transition to renewable electricity is also expected to ease pressure on the regional power grid, improve energy self-sufficiency for participating factories and deliver annual cost savings of nearly VND 3.5 billion. The successful commissioning and initial stable supply to the three industrial facilities provide a foundation for VinEnergo to expand its green energy activities in subsequent phases. The company aims to develop an integrated energy model combining renewable generation, large-scale battery storage, electricity distribution and retail infrastructure to support growing industrial demand in the Vung Ang Economic Zone. Nguyen Huong Giang, Deputy General Director of VinEnergo, said the project represents an important step towards developing a comprehensive energy ecosystem covering renewable generation, storage, DPPA mechanisms and electricity distribution. She highlighted the company’s focus on applying Vietnamese-developed products, manufacturing capabilities and technology to address the energy requirements of industrial customers. Beyond this project, VinEnergo is providing BESS solutions for several major projects of Hanoi Power Corporation and Northern Power Corporation, with a combined capacity exceeding 1.1 GWh. Internationally, the company has announced a renewable energy project portfolio totalling 10 GW and is implementing its first projects in Asia and Europe. VinEnergo aims to expand its project portfolio to 100 GW within the next three years, positioning itself among the world’s leading renewable energy companies. artigo.texto: SHANGHAI, Nov. 02, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Sigenergy, a global pioneer in next-generation energy storage solutions, has just been designated as a Tier 1 Energy Storage Manufacturer by BloombergNEF (BNEF) for the fourth quarter of 2026. This prestigious benchmark highlights Sigenergy’s exceptional financial stability, robust bankability, and field-proven product reliability across major global markets. BloombergNEF’s Tier 1 rating is widely recognized as one of the most rigorous independent evaluation frameworks in the renewable energy sector. Designed to provide transparent market intelligence, the Tier 1 designation assesses manufacturers based on stringent criteria including financial health, demonstrated project delivery track records, and strict quality standards. For global investors, Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) contractors, project developers, and asset owners, Sigenergy’s Tier 1 status offers strong assurance of long-term operational stability and technical performance, facilitating smoother project financing and risk mitigation across the energy value chain. The Tier 1 status validates Sigenergy’s rapid worldwide growth, fueled by continuous R&D investment and its visionary "AI in All" strategy. By integrating artificial intelligence into its flexible, modular product architecture, Sigenergy delivers highly reliable, innovative energy storage solutions tailored for diverse applications, ranging from Commercial & Industrial (C&I) projects to complex, utility-scale power plants. This milestone reinforces Sigenergy’s commitment to empowering a broader spectrum of global customers, asset owners, and partners with scalable efficiency, robust safety, and long-term project value. About Sigenergy Founded in 2022 and headquartered in Shanghai, Sigenergy (6656.HK) is a technology-driven company focused on innovation in the new energy sector. Leveraging advanced digital intelligence and a highly skilled talent base, the company has expanded across photovoltaic(PV)generation, smart energy storage and high-efficiency electric vehicle (EV) charging solutions. Guided by its "AI in All” strategy, Sigenergy integrates artificial intelligence across its product ecosystem to deliver safer, smarter and more efficient energy solutions for households and businesses worldwide. For more information, visit: www.sigenergy.com Media Contact Tracy Li Email: [email protected] A photo accompanying this announcement is available at https://www.globenewswire.com/NewsRoom/AttachmentNg/df0a94ea-9736-49f7-8fc7-9146ad7fbd21

artigo.texto: Solidus Techno Power Delivers 27.31 MWh BESS for 50 MW Solar Project 02 Nov 2026 2 Min Read CW Team Share Solidus Techno Power has delivered a 27.31 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) integrated with a 50 MW solar project for SBF Ispat. The company provided comprehensive engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) services for the project, expanding its presence across integrated renewable energy and storage solutions. The delivery strengthens Solidus Techno Power’s solar and energy storage portfolio. It also supports the company’s broader strategy of combining renewable energy development and EPC capabilities with battery storage manufacturing through its subsidiary XenRosh ESS. Solidus said the project represents a milestone in its expansion into integrated solar and energy storage solutions. The company is positioning storage alongside solar generation as part of its offering to customers seeking to use renewable power more effectively and manage energy requirements with greater flexibility. Jaspal Singh, chief executive officer and co-founder of Solidus Techno Power, said the combination of solar power and battery storage could give industries greater flexibility in using renewable energy. His comments highlighted the role of storage in improving the practical use of power generated from solar projects. Harvinder Singh, managing director of Solidus Techno Power, said the project had strengthened the company’s integrated clean-energy portfolio. He added that XenRosh ESS was expanding its BESS manufacturing capabilities with a focus on quality, safety and reliability. Through XenRosh ESS, Solidus is developing manufacturing capabilities for battery energy storage systems to serve the expanding market. The subsidiary’s activities complement Solidus’s EPC and renewable energy development businesses, giving the group an integrated presence across project execution, energy generation and storage equipment manufacturing. artigo.texto: CATL Returns 19.37 Million Shares to Treasury as Brokerages Rethink the Growth Story Published on 11/01/2026 at 05:52 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL has bought back 19.37 million A-shares between September 11 and Wednesday, the battery maker disclosed in a regulatory filing. Wednesday alone accounted for 0.87 million shares, acquired for RMB 199.98 million. The repurchase programme has unfolded against a backdrop of disappointing quarterly figures and mounting competitive pressure that has weighed on the stock. A Quarter That Missed on Both Lines For the third quarter of 2026, CATL reported an unaudited net profit of RMB 21.2 billion, up 14.5% year on year. Revenue climbed 58.6% to RMB 165.2 billion. Neither figure cleared what analysts had pencilled in — consensus had pointed to profit growth of 41.2%. Reuters described the earnings expansion as the weakest in nearly two years, pointing to fiercer competition in batteries and slower growth in Chinese car sales. The shortfall triggered a sharp slide in the share price, with the disappointing results, intensifying battery-market rivalry and softer vehicle demand all cited as triggers. By Friday the stock had recovered some ground, adding 1.7%. Morgan Stanley Steps Back, UOB Trims Its Numbers Morgan Stanley downgraded CATL's H-shares to "In-Line" on Tuesday, according to media reports, and cut its price target by 44.7% to HK$390. UOB Kay Hian had moved two days earlier, on October 22, keeping its buy recommendation on the A-shares but lowering its target to RMB470.00 from RMB585.00. The Singapore-based house also trimmed its net profit forecasts for 2026 through 2028, by 5%, 10% and 16% respectively, expecting CATL to absorb part of higher taxes. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? Swapping Batteries, Not Chemistries While the analysts were marking down their models, CATL pressed ahead on the product front. Reuters reported on October 21 that the company unveiled its Tianxing II battery platform, with plans for 900 battery-swap stations for heavy trucks across China by year-end and 2,000 by 2027. The passenger-car side is expanding through partnerships: on October 22, CATL reportedly agreed with Beijing Automotive Group to develop a swap system serving one million vehicles, with BAIC contributing compatible models to the Choco-Swap network and supporting station roll-out through its dealerships. On the technology roadmap, CATL told investors on Tuesday that work on all-solid-state batteries remains on schedule, with small-series production targeted for 2027. artigo.texto: Rainha de bateria da Unidos da Tijuca, Mileide Mihaile celebra enredo ligado às suas raízes nordestinas Maranhense de Imperatriz, influenciadora comenta a proposta da escola para 2027, inspirada na literatura, na fé e nas tradições populares Por O Globo — Rio de Janeiro Atualizado Após anunciar, em maio, que deixaria o posto de rainha de bateria da Unidos da Tijuca, Mileide Mihaile confirmou que continuará à frente da Pura Cadência no Carnaval de 2027. A influenciadora e empresária conseguiu conciliar os compromissos pessoais e profissionais que haviam motivado o afastamento e chegou a um novo acordo com a direção da escola. Nesta quinta-feira (29), ela reencontrou a comunidade tijucana durante o primeiro ensaio de rua para o próximo desfile. A permanência foi definida após conversas com a direção da agremiação e ajustes na agenda. Segundo Mileide, embora tenha considerado necessário se afastar naquele momento, a vontade de continuar sempre esteve presente. "Naquele momento, eu tinha algumas questões pessoais que precisavam da minha atenção e não queria assumir um compromisso sem ter certeza de que conseguiria me dedicar como gostaria. Felizmente, as coisas foram se organizando, conseguimos fazer alguns ajustes e surgiu a possibilidade de continuar. Fiquei muito feliz, porque tenho um carinho enorme pela Tijuca e pela comunidade", afirma. A relação com os ritmistas e os integrantes da escola também pesou na decisão. Ao longo de sua trajetória na Unidos da Tijuca, a influenciadora diz ter construído vínculos que ultrapassam os compromissos da temporada carnavalesca. "O carinho nunca mudou. Tenho uma admiração enorme pelos ritmistas, pela dedicação de cada um e por tudo o que fazem pela escola. Essas relações vão muito além do Carnaval, porque a gente compartilha momentos e cria uma proximidade verdadeira. Estou muito feliz por continuar essa história e quero aproveitar cada momento ao lado da minha Pura Cadência", conta. Para o desfile de 2027, a agremiação levará à Marquês de Sapucaí o enredo "A Cabeça do Santo", inspirado no livro homônimo da escritora Socorro Acioli. A proposta reúne referências à literatura brasileira, à fé e às crenças populares, temas com os quais Mileide se identifica também por sua origem nordestina. "Eu achei uma escolha muito bonita. O que mais me encanta nesse enredo é justamente essa mistura da literatura com a fé, as crenças populares e as tradições do nosso povo. Acho incrível pensar que uma história pode ganhar vida na avenida e alcançar milhões de pessoas através do carnaval. Tenho certeza de que será um desfile muito especial", destaca. Natural de Imperatriz, no Maranhão, Mileide vê na apresentação uma oportunidade de valorizar as referências culturais que fazem parte de sua história. Para ela, ocupar esse espaço na festa é também uma forma de dar visibilidade às tradições da região onde nasceu. "Eu saí de Imperatriz levando comigo tudo o que vivi no Maranhão: nossa cultura, nossas festas, nossa música e nossas tradições. São coisas que fazem parte de quem eu sou. O Nordeste tem histórias lindas que merecem ser conhecidas, e gosto muito de poder representar essa região, mostrando que uma mulher nordestina pode conquistar seus espaços sem deixar suas raízes para trás", diz. Com a permanência definida, a preparação para o próximo desfile também entra em uma nova etapa. Mileide pretende intensificar os treinos físicos, com atenção à resistência e ao condicionamento necessários para acompanhar a sequência de ensaios e a apresentação na avenida. Fora da rotina da escola, ela mantém os projetos profissionais, entre eles a próxima edição do Bazar Mulher, iniciativa voltada ao empreendedorismo e ao apoio a outras mulheres.

Após o fechamento de 29 de outubro, o The Information informou que a Nvidia está em negociações para garantir bilhões de dólares em dívida para um data center da Nscale que a Anthropic planeja usar. O fluxo de caixa do trimestre de julho, que ficou abaixo da metade da estimativa do mercado, diz mais sobre o custo desse alcance. As ações caíram 1,17% em 28 de outubro e 4,22% para $204,64 em 30 de outubro, a primeira sessão após o relatório da Nscale. artigo.texto: Energy Storage Briefs: 1.NVVN's First 250 MW/500 MWh BESS Project In Rajasthan Goes Commercial Nearly two years after the tender was issued, IndiGrid and EnerGrid have commissioned a 250 MW / 500 MWh standalone Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) in Rajasthan through Rajasthan BESS Private Limited (RBPL). The project adds to India's growing battery storage capacity as the country looks to improve grid flexibility and integrate a larger share of renewable energy. NTPC Vidyut Vyapar Nigam Limited (NVVN) issued the tender in June 2024 for 1 GWh of standalone battery storage capacity with viability gap funding (VGF) support. IndiGrid secured 500 MWh, or half of the total tendered capacity, in October 2024 at a quoted tariff of approximately ₹2.37 lakh/MW/month. 2. Pakistan Finally Moves to Add Storage, Pushed By Unplanned Solar To The Grid Pakistan imported more than 4.5 GW of battery storage equipment in the first half of 2026, nearly half of everything it has ever imported, a Pakistan Solar Association representative told a parliamentary dialogue on long-term energy planning, as reported on 29 October. The association quoted the figure in gigawatts, whereas storage is usually tallied in gigawatt-hours, and it does not reconcile neatly with other trackers, so it is best read as indicative of scale rather than precise. Battery maker CATL has launched its 9 MWh TENER+ energy storage system at All-Energy Australia in Melbourne which its claims would require 40% fewer containers and has a 35% smaller footprint than conventional designs. CATL also showcased its TENER Sodium system in Australia for the first time and signed three memoranda of understanding (MoUs) with Hitachi Energy, EPEC Group and the University of New South Wales. The product represents an engineering advance, while the agreements address the commercial challenges of project delivery.

artigo.texto: Sam Altman diz ser “terrível” ter muita memória RAM em computadores pessoais em vez de data centers Declaração ocorre em meio a uma escassez global de memória RAM, resultado do aumento da demanda por chips em diferentes setores da tecnologia, especialmente com a expansão dos data centers voltados à inteligência artificial O CEO da OpenAI, Sam Altman, afirmou ser “terrível” ter muita memória RAM em computadores pessoais em vez de data centers. Segundo o The Verge, durante sua participação no podcast Cheeky Pint, divulgado nesta semana, o executivo foi questionado sobre a escassez de componentes na cadeia de suprimentos, como a atual falta de memória RAM. “Muitas pessoas querem fazer inferência local. E, de alguma forma, elas presumem que o problema está resolvido agora porque teremos modelos de código aberto, poderemos executá-los em nossos computadores e, assim, não precisaremos de todas aquelas coisas nos data centers", disse. "Mas, do ponto de vista de alocação global, na verdade, é bastante terrível que todo mundo tenha uma boa quantidade do estoque limitado de DRAM [tipo mais comum de memória RAM] do mundo em seu próprio computador, sendo usada 5% do tempo", afirmou Altman. "Você quer a máxima utilização na nuvem se está tentando lidar com esse ambiente de oferta muito restrita. E, de alguma forma, a intuição de todos — de muitas pessoas — é o contrário disso", complementou. A declaração ocorre em meio à escassez global de memória RAM, em um cenário de forte disputa por esses componentes. Segundo o The Verge, fabricantes como Samsung e SK Hynix têm contratos de longo prazo com empresas que operam serviços de computação em nuvem, responsáveis por grandes data centers. Projetos como o Stargate, da OpenAI, também reservaram grande parte da produção mundial de RAM para os próximos anos. A forte demanda das empresas de tecnologia por chips para abastecer seus data centers aumenta a disputa por componentes que também são utilizados em computadores e celulares. Com a oferta limitada, essa concorrência pressiona os preços da memória e pode encarecer os produtos eletrônicos.

artigo.texto: The Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission (GERC) has officially notified the Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission (Grid Interactive Distributed Renewable Energy Sources) Regulations, 2026, introducing a comprehensive framework for grid-connected distributed renewable energy systems across the state. Issued under Notification No. 11 of 2026, the new regulations replace the Net Metering Rooftop Solar PV Grid Interactive Systems Regulations, 2016, and establish updated provisions for residential, commercial and industrial consumers adopting distributed renewable energy sources (DRES). The regulations introduce five metering mechanisms: Net Metering, Net Billing, Gross Metering, Group Net Metering and Virtual Net Metering. Under Net Metering and Net Billing, consumers can install systems with capacities ranging from 1 kW AC to 1,000 kW AC or 1,250 kWp DC. Gross Metering systems can have capacities between 6 kW AC and 4,000 kW AC. Group Net Metering allows consumers to share generated electricity across multiple connections belonging to the same entity and consumer category, with a maximum capacity of 1,000 kW AC. Virtual Net Metering provides another option for collective renewable energy adoption, enabling energy sharing across different locations within the jurisdiction of the same distribution licensee. Systems under this arrangement can range from 10 kW AC to 4,000 kW AC, allowing multiple consumers to benefit from renewable electricity generated at a common location. To address grid stability and manage additional renewable energy generation, GERC has introduced mandatory Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) integration requirements for certain consumers. Prosumers with contract demand exceeding 100 kW who intend to install DRES capacity beyond their sanctioned demand must incorporate battery storage. The storage system must support at least two hours of charging and discharging per day for a minimum of 50% of the excess DRES capacity. The regulations also establish different energy settlement mechanisms for residential and non-residential consumers. Residential prosumers under Net Metering will receive 100% adjustment of exported electricity against their grid consumption without banking charges. Any annual surplus energy remaining after adjustment will be purchased by distribution companies at ₹2.25 per kWh. For non-residential consumers, energy adjustment is limited to 30% of total imported electricity during each billing cycle and is subject to applicable banking charges. Any excess electricity injected beyond the permitted adjustment will be treated as lapsed energy. GERC has also prescribed technical and safety requirements for grid-connected systems. All installations must comply with Central Electricity Authority (CEA) standards and the Gujarat Electricity Grid Code. Mandatory anti-islanding protection and automatic isolation devices will ensure safe grid operation. Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) meters with RS-485 ports or advanced communication capabilities will also be required for monitoring electricity flows. Monitoring requirements will depend on project capacity. Systems exceeding 1 MW must install Remote Terminal Units (RTUs), while installations below 1 MW will require SIM-based remote monitoring systems. For implementation, distribution licensees must establish dedicated online portals to manage consumer registrations, applications, processing and approvals within specified timelines. Connectivity charges will range from ₹1,500 for smaller 1–6 kW systems to ₹50,000 for larger installations of up to 4 MW. Additionally, consumers will retain 100% of the carbon credit benefits generated through their systems, while electricity produced under the framework will contribute towards DISCOMs’ Renewable Purchase Obligations (RPO). With the introduction of these regulations, Gujarat has established updated provisions for distributed renewable energy generation, electricity sharing, battery storage integration and grid connectivity across different consumer categories. artigo.texto: CATL Pairs Australian Storage Debut With Sodium-Ion and Swap Push as Margins Face Scrutiny Published on 11/01/2026 at 23:30 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL used the All Energy Australia stage in Melbourne to give its TENER+ energy storage system its global premiere on Thursday, unveiling a unit rated at 9 MWh. Alongside the launch, media reports said the company signed letters of intent with Hitachi Energy, EPEC Group and UNSW Sydney aimed at backing large-scale battery storage projects across Australia. The Australian showcase is only one strand of a broader push. At the start of November, CATL moved to deepen its bet on energy storage and battery swapping, creating a storage subsidiary with planned registered capital of RMB 5 billion. The vehicle's business plan also takes in AI software. A sodium-ion venture with Intilion, sized at 3 GWh, rounds out the announcements. Those figures describe how the subsidiary will be funded, not the revenue or profit it will generate — a distinction worth keeping in mind when weighing the expansion. Crowded Ground WaterRock Energy Economics reckons competition in the targeted segments is already fierce. In storage, CATL runs into BYD; in battery swapping, Nio stands in the way. The expansion, in other words, does not lead into unoccupied territory. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? Carmakers, meanwhile, are lining up alternative cell suppliers. Li Auto took a RMB 2.65 billion stake in Sunwoda Power in September and holds 8.32% of the company. Xiaomi also bought in. The two automakers run a joint battery venture, and the latest-generation Li Auto L8 uses Sunwoda cells exclusively. Such moves matter to CATL because they strengthen rival supply relationships. Back in 2023, the company offered selected automakers lithium carbonate at RMB 200,000 per tonne, provided they sourced roughly 80% of their battery needs from CATL over three years. The Sunwoda investments show that carmakers are charting their own courses alongside — or instead of — such long-term commitments, raising the value to CATL of sales channels beyond its established customer base. Technology Pipeline Solid-state batteries remain a priority. CATL told investors on Tuesday that it will keep funding the technology, with small-series production targeted for 2027. On swapping, the company agreed on 22 October to deepen cooperation with the BAIC Group. According to media reports, the signed accord covers adapting several BAIC brands to CATL's swap system, with the partners also planning to build out the associated network. There was a legal reprieve in Hungary as well. A court on Friday dismissed a lawsuit brought by residents against the Debrecen battery plant, Reuters reported, on the grounds that the plaintiffs lost standing after the permitting documents were revised. The court also found no regulatory breaches in the approval process, according to the report. The ruling removes a legal burden less than a month after trial production began. CATL at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. Earnings Lag Revenue Third-quarter 2026 figures showed revenue of RMB 165.22 billion, up 58.6% year on year. Net profit attributable to shareholders came in at RMB 21.25 billion, a gain of 14.5% — meaning earnings growth trailed the top line. Brokers have taken note. Morgan Stanley has flagged pressure from price competition, and Nomura cut its CATL profit forecasts for 2026–2028 in October by as much as 10.2%. The new business lines thus answer economic pressure without yet proving it has been overcome. Storage and swapping widen CATL's footprint, but whether that translates into profitable growth depends on how the company holds its own against entrenched rivals. For investors, the gap between announced expansion and hard earnings contributions is where the real test lies. Ad CATL Stock: New Analysis - 1 November Fresh CATL information released. artigo.texto: Principais Estatísticas para a Ação da AMD - Preço Atual: $504.80 - Preço-Alvo (Médio): ~$2,340 - Alvo da Rua: ~$640 - Retorno Total Potencial: ~363% - TIR Anualizada: ~44% / ano O Que Aconteceu? Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) caiu 10,88% para $504,80 em 30 de outubro, dias antes de seu próprio relatório em 3 de novembro. O gatilho foi a Intel (INTC), que revisou sua previsão de receita para o quarto trimestre para $15,0 bilhões a $16,0 bilhões e fechou em queda de 28,58%. No entanto, o mesmo relatório mostrou a receita da Intel com data centers subindo 78%, e os data centers representaram 58% da receita da AMD no segundo trimestre. O Philadelphia Semiconductor Index caiu mais de 7% e a Nvidia 4,22%, com os planos de gastos com IA da Amazon adicionando às preocupações. A AMD caiu mais do que ambas, pois os investidores reavaliaram sua exposição à mesma fraqueza do mercado de PCs. A Intel Vendeu Menos PCs e Servidores Mais Caros "Olhando para frente, vemos a desaceleração do PC continuando pelo menos até a primeira metade do próximo ano", disse o CFO da Intel, David Zinsner. O grupo de clientes e IA física da Intel caiu 5% para $8,1 bilhões, e a Intel espera que a receita com clientes caia mais de 20% em relação ao terceiro trimestre. O lado dos data centers seguiu na direção oposta. A receita com data centers e IA subiu 78% para $7,3 bilhões, e o 10-Q da Intel credita o ganho nos servidores aos preços médios de venda, que subiram 54%. A Intel espera que a divisão cresça em uma porcentagem de dois dígitos médios de forma sequencial no quarto trimestre, embora uma escassez de substratos de embalagem esteja limitando a velocidade com que pode aumentar a produção de servidores. A Receita da AMD Está no Lado que Está Crescendo A receita da AMD com data centers mais do que dobrou para $6,7 bilhões no segundo trimestre, enquanto a receita com clientes subiu 23% para $3,1 bilhões, cerca de 27% das vendas. A Intel também é a principal rival da AMD em servidores, então seu crescimento de 78% fala sobre a força da demanda, não sobre quem está ganhando market share. A queda do mercado de PCs ainda custa algo à AMD. artigo.texto: LG CNS has completed a 30-megawatt artificial intelligence data center in Jakarta, Indonesia, marking the first overseas AI data center built by a Korean company for a foreign client, with its entire capacity booked before completion. The facility was commissioned last year by KMG, a joint venture between Indonesia's Sinar Mas Group and Korea Investment Real Asset Management. The project marks LG CNS' entry into overseas AI data center construction for third-party clients. Designed to support next-generation graphics processing units and high-performance computing, the center features a hybrid cooling system combining conventional air cooling with liquid cooling to handle heat generated by AI servers. The initial phase uses air cooling, with liquid cooling to be introduced in a subsequent phase. The facility's power infrastructure can support more than 300 kilowatts per rack, roughly 60 times the capacity of a conventional data center rack. Redundant power systems ensure continued operations in the event of a primary power failure. The project also brings together technologies from LG affiliates under the group's integrated "One LG" strategy, combining LG CNS' data center design, construction and operation capabilities with cooling systems from LG Electronics and batteries from LG Energy Solution. LG CNS is already designing the next phase of the project, which aims to expand the facility's total power capacity to 400 MW. Building on its Indonesian foothold, the company plans to pursue AI data center projects in Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines and Japan, as demand for AI computing infrastructure accelerates across Asia. In Korea, LG CNS offers data center colocation, design-build-operate services, modular facilities, GPU-as-a-service and liquid cooling solutions. It also plans to expand into AI factory services by integrating its infrastructure capabilities with AI platforms and applications. "The completion of the Indonesian data center demonstrates our ability to deliver our expertise to overseas clients and compete in global markets," LG CNS CEO Hyun Shin-Gyoon said. "We will use this project as a stepping-stone to expand our AI data center and AI factory businesses across the Asia-Pacific region and beyond." jyoungseon8@heraldcorp.com

artigo.texto: [PRNewswire] LONGi Energy Storage Showcases Full-Stack Capabilities MELBOURNE, Australia Oct. 31, 2026 /PRNewswire=YONHAP/ -- LONGi Energy Storage showcased its utility-scale, commercial and industrial (C&I), and microgrid solutions at All Energy Australia 2026, demonstrating its integrated capabilities across diverse energy applications. Under its LONGi ONE strategy, LONGi Energy Storage continues to advance technology innovation and localized services to support Australia's energy transition. Solutions for Diverse Energy Applications As Australia expands renewable energy deployment, energy storage is increasingly important for grid flexibility, energy cost optimization and reliable power supply. OneMatrix Solution addresses utility-scale applications, including renewable energy projects, standalone grid-side storage and electricity market operations. Featuring flexible modular design and LONGiBank 3.0, it supports 2–8-hour duration and customized system configurations. Cluster-level independent management, AI-powered battery health diagnostics and intelligent O&M help improve operational efficiency and support long-term asset performance. The solution has received TÜV Rheinland certifications under IEC 62619, IEC 63056, and an IEC/EN 60730-1 Annex H report, reinforcing its safety credentials for international markets. Hi-MO One Pro supports C&I applications with flexible 2-24-hour configurations for solar-plus-storage, peak-valley arbitrage, and backup power. Featuring LONGi's proprietary iCCS and liquid-cooling technology, it supports grid-connected and off-grid operation, helping businesses optimize energy costs and enhance power supply security. OneNexus H2 and M5 serve remote areas, mining operations and other locations with limited grid access. By coordinating solar, battery storage and diesel generation, they help increase renewable energy utilization, reduce diesel dependence and strengthen power supply resilience. Project Experience Demonstrates Local Market Value In Strathalbyn, South Australia, the Lunio Energy BESS project was connected to the grid in September 2026. Comprising four LONGiBank 2.0 systems with a total capacity of 5 MW/20 MWh, the project participates in Australia's National Electricity Market (NEM), optimizing charging and discharging in response to electricity demand and market prices. Advancing LONGi ONE Through Localized Services LONGi continues to integrate proprietary technologies, system solutions and intelligent O&M under its LONGi ONE strategy, providing support from solution design and delivery through lifecycle operations. Through its "2830 Plan," LONGi aims to establish 30 comprehensive local service centers worldwide by the end of 2028, strengthening local responsiveness and lifecycle support. With its full-stack capabilities, diverse solution portfolio and expanding local service network, LONGi Energy Storage will continue working with Australian customers and partners to deliver flexible, reliable and sustainable energy solutions. artigo.texto: MELBOURNE, Australia, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Aeson Power demonstrated the versatility of sodium-ion technology across energy storage and automotive applications at All Energy Australia 2026, held at the Melbourne Convention and Exhibition Centre. At Booth G101, the company presented its latest solutions, highlighting sodium-ion technology's growing role in Australia's energy storage market. Aeson Power's Sodium battery in All-Energy Flexible Sodium-Ion Solutions for Residential Energy Storage A key feature was the APSI2500-based sodium-ion battery system, designed for residential energy storage applications. Combining sodium-ion batteries with Aeson Power's proprietary Ecocase and Ecocab components, the system supports flexible capacity configurations to meet different household energy storage needs. With sodium-ion technology's safety advantages and wide-temperature operating capabilities, the system offers households a flexible energy storage option with safety as a key consideration. Intelligent Energy Storage for Commercial and Industrial Applications Aeson Power also presented the HaloDyne Na 120/119, an all-in-one liquid-cooled sodium-ion energy storage system for commercial and industrial applications. Its sodium-ion chemistry and multi-level fire protection are designed to enhance system safety. With 1C high-rate charging and discharging, the system delivers up to twice the rated power of a comparable 0.5C system with the same battery capacity. This makes it well suited to peak demand management, multi-peak energy arbitrage, and microgrid frequency regulation, where high power output can help reduce the battery capacity needed for specific applications and improve space efficiency. Sodium-Ion Technology for Automotive Starting Applications The exhibition also featured the NaForce sodium-ion starter battery series, demonstrating the growing commercial adoption of sodium-ion technology in the automotive sector. As part of Aeson Power's established product portfolio, NaForce reflects the company's efforts to bring sodium-ion innovation into practical, real-world automotive applications. Together, the three product lines illustrated the versatility of sodium-ion technology, from flexible residential energy storage configurations to integrated commercial energy storage and automotive starting solutions. Through continued product development, Aeson Power aims to deliver reliable performance, safety-conscious design, and flexible integration across evolving energy and automotive markets. Aeson Power's sodium-ion solutions attracted strong interest from visitors at All Energy Australia 2026, prompting engaging discussions with industry professionals throughout the exhibition. About Aeson Power Aeson Power is an Australian pioneer in next-generation battery technology, serving global automotive and energy markets with advanced sodium-ion solutions. Aeson Power designs, develops, and markets high-reliability battery solutions for automotive, energy storage, and more. For more information, visit www.aesonpower.com PR Newswire Asia Ltd. artigo.texto: The world's largest 60-MW liquid air energy storage project in Golmud, Northwest China's Qinghai Province Photo: Courtesy of CGDG A 60-megawatt (MW) liquid air energy storage project in Northwest China was connected to the grid and started generating power on Friday, marking a major breakthrough in the engineering and commercialization of liquid air energy storage technology, CCTV News reported on Saturday. The project, located in Golmud, Northwest China's Qinghai Province, was invested in and built by China Green Development Investment Group (CGDG) and is now the worldâs largest liquid air energy storage facility by installed capacity, the company said. The project marks a milestone in Chinaâs push to develop storage technologies that can help support a power system with a growing share of renewable energy. The facility has a total installed capacity of 60 MW and is expected to absorb about 600,000 kilowatt-hours of clean electricity a day, according to the company. It is projected to generate around 180 million kilowatt-hours each year, enough to meet the annual electricity demand of roughly 30,000 households. Liquid air energy storage is an emerging long-duration storage technology that uses electricity to compress and cool air until it becomes liquid during periods of low demand. When power is needed, the liquid air is warmed and expanded to drive turbines and generate electricity. The technology does not require the geographic conditions needed for pumped hydro storage and is seen as having advantages over batteries in scale, storage duration and service life. CGDG said the Golmud project uses a deep-cooling liquefaction process at minus 194 degrees Celsius and has achieved full domestic localization of equipment, with 100 percent of components made in China. The company also said the project incorporates technology over which it holds independent intellectual property rights. The company said the project ranks first globally in both storage power and storage capacity in the liquid air energy storage sector. Ji Wei, chief engineer at CGDG, said the project had completed the full process of âcompression, liquefaction, storage and power generationâ and achieved coordinated scheduling of cold, heat, electricity, and gas flows, according to CCTV News. During construction, the project team developed several large-scale pieces of equipment, including the worldâs largest horizontally split centrifugal compressor and a liquid expander with the largest single-unit flow rate, Ji said. The project is expected to support renewable energy absorption, peak shaving for thermal power plants and the use of liquefied natural gas cold energy, according to the company. With the project now online, China is moving a step closer to building a new-type power system in which new energy serves as the mainstay of supply, according to analysts. It fills multiple gaps in large-scale engineering applications of liquid air energy storage worldwide, offering a replicable model for the scaled application of long-duration storage technology and the cultivation of a complete industrial chain â a significant step toward China's dual carbon goals. Chinaâs installed capacity of new energy storage reached 136 gigawatts by the end of 2025, marking an 84 percent increase year-on-year and a massive 40-fold expansion compared to the end of 2020, according to a report issued by the National Energy Administration. artigo.texto: LG CNS has secured lease agreements for 100% of its artificial intelligence (AI) data center capacity in Indonesia ahead of completion. Meanwhile, the company said it would invest gradually in its graphics processing unit (GPU) services business after assessing demand and commercial viability. During its third-quarter earnings conference call on Oct. 30, LG CNS announced that its AI data center in Jakarta, Indonesia, is scheduled for completion in early November. The company added that the facility has already secured tenants for its entire capacity. “We secured customers to lease the entire facility before completion, establishing a stable revenue base from the start of operations,” said Yoo Ki-woong, vice president of LG CNS’ AI and Cloud Business Division, during the conference call. He explained that the company is pursuing additional data center construction projects in Indonesia and exploring expansion into North America and Europe. The Indonesian data center is LG CNS’ first overseas AI data center construction project. In 2024, the company signed a data center consulting and design contract with local operator KMG. It subsequently secured a 100 billion won infrastructure construction contract in August 2025. KMG is a joint venture established by Indonesia’s Sinar Mas Group and Korea Investment Real Asset Management. LG CNS participated in the project through LG Sinar Mas Technology Solutions, its joint venture with Sinar Mas Group. The first-phase data center has 11 above-ground floors, a total floor area of 46,281 square meters and a power intake capacity of 30 megawatts (MW). It can accommodate more than 100,000 servers. Project owner KMG plans to expand total power intake capacity to 220 MW. In North America and Europe, LG CNS plans to focus on prefabricated modular data centers. “We are pursuing business cooperation through our U.S. subsidiary and local partners,” Yoo said. “We plan to enter the market using modular data center technology designed to support Nvidia’s next-generation AI platform, Vera Rubin.” According to the company, the modular approach reduces on-site construction work compared with conventional methods and allows facilities to be expanded in stages according to customer demand. However, LG CNS intends to manage investment risks in its GPU services business separately from its broader AI infrastructure expansion. LG CNS chief financial officer (CFO) Song Kwang-ryun expressed a positive view of the medium- to long-term growth potential of GPU-as-a-Service (GPUaaS) during the conference call. He said the company is reviewing business opportunities involving LG Group affiliates and external enterprises but must consider the substantial upfront investment costs and rapid pace of technological change. “We will proceed cautiously, focusing on projects with established commercial viability,” Song said of future investments. LG CNS previously decided at a Sept. 11 board meeting to invest 381.4 billion won in GPUs and infrastructure equipment, including Nvidia’s Vera Rubin. The equipment acquisition is scheduled for June 30, 2027. The company appears to intend to determine the scale of future GPUaaS investments based on actual demand and profitability, separately from the GPU investment already approved. GPUs require substantial upfront capital, and rapid equipment replacement cycles mean customer acquisition and utilization rates can significantly affect investment returns. Meanwhile, AI and cloud revenue reached 961.5 billion won in the third quarter, accounting for 57.8% of LG CNS’ total revenue of 1.6643 trillion won.
