artigo.texto: Marketing Bago’s carbon market initiative at COP31 By Aliyu Umar Aliyu As global climate diplomacy shifts from promises to practical implementation, Niger State has an opportunity to position its emerging carbon market initiative as a vehicle for investment, job creation and sustainable development. For Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago, popularly known as the Farmer Governor, the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), scheduled for November 9–20, 2026, in Antalya, Türkiye, offers a strategic platform to advance the state’s green economy vision. The conference will bring together governments, investors, climate finance institutions, development partners and environmental experts to discuss practical responses to climate change. For Niger State, however, participation should go beyond showcasing its environmental ambitions. The priority should be to secure credible partnerships, develop investment-ready projects and establish a clear pathway for converting its natural resources into measurable climate and economic benefits. Governor Bago’s vision presents an opportunity to connect climate action with Niger State’s agricultural strength, forest resources, renewable energy potential and waste-management needs. If properly developed, these assets could support projects that reduce greenhouse gas emissions while creating employment, improving energy access and strengthening rural livelihoods. Niger State’s participation at COP29 in Baku, Azerbaijan, in November 2024 provided an earlier opportunity to promote its green economy agenda, including sustainable agriculture, renewable energy and forest conservation. COP31 should build on that engagement by moving from international advocacy towards practical project development and investment mobilisation. From Green Economy Vision to Carbon Market Investment Carbon markets provide a potential mechanism for financing projects that reduce or remove greenhouse gas emissions. Under recognised crediting systems, a carbon credit generally represents one metric tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent reduced or removed, subject to the applicable methodology and verification requirements. For Niger State, opportunities could include methane capture at landfills, climate-smart rice cultivation, solar mini-grids and forest restoration. These initiatives could attract investors while supporting the state’s wider development objectives. However, natural resources alone do not guarantee carbon revenue. Projects must demonstrate credible emissions reductions, additionality, appropriate monitoring and independent verification. They must also comply with relevant national regulations and international carbon market requirements. This is particularly important as Niger State seeks to position itself as a pioneer in subnational carbon market development in Nigeria. The ambition to become the country’s first subnational government to open its carbon market to investment, and to advance towards international carbon-credit sales, could be significant. The proposed Niger State Carbon Market Office could play a central role by coordinating project identification, technical assessments, investor engagement, regulatory compliance and stakeholder participation. Its effectiveness will depend on a clear mandate, adequate expertise, transparent procedures and coordination with the relevant federal authorities. International cooperation could accelerate this process. In correspondence to the Niger State team concerning a post-feasibility mission action plan, myclimate’s Article 6 Bilateral Cooperation Team disclosed that a draft memorandum of understanding (MoU) on project development and carbon market activities was undergoing internal legal review, with the intention of finalising it before COP31. The correspondence, signed on behalf of the team by Nsikan-George Emana, Senior Project Manager for Bilateral Cooperation at myclimate, proposed November 12, 2026, for a strategic meeting with the Niger State Government, during which the parties hope to sign the agreement. The proposed engagement offers an opportunity to establish a framework for technical cooperation, project development and potential international market participation. Nevertheless, the MoU remains prospective until formally concluded, and its existence should not be mistaken for evidence that investment has already been secured or carbon credits sold. Niger State should approach the meeting with clearly defined priorities, including project timelines, financing arrangements, responsibilities, community safeguards and measurable implementation targets. Article 6 and the International Opportunity The proposed partnership is particularly relevant to Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, which provides frameworks for international cooperation in reducing greenhouse gas emissions. At COP29 in November 2024, countries made significant progress on the rules governing international carbon trading and the UN-supervised carbon crediting mechanism. Under Article 6.2, countries can cooperate through internationally transferred mitigation outcomes, subject to applicable accounting and authorisation requirements. Article 6.4 provides a UN-supervised crediting mechanism, while Article 6.8 addresses non-market approaches. For Niger State, these frameworks could create opportunities to develop projects that attract international finance and contribute to Nigeria’s climate commitments. However, the state must work within Nigeria’s national climate governance arrangements. International transfers under Article 6 cannot be treated as an exclusively state-level transaction where national authorisation and accounting are required. Potential projects should therefore be developed with appropriate technical, legal and financial support. Inaugurado na noite desta quinta-feira (29), o Data Center Sebrae Senador Fernando Bezerra está instalado na sede do Sebrae-RN, em Natal, e será responsável pelo armazenamento e processamento de dados de 12 unidades estaduais do Sistema Sebrae, localizadas nas regiões Nordeste, Norte e Sudeste. A estrutura amplia a capacidade tecnológica da instituição e reforça as estratégias de segurança da informação e transformação digital dos pequenos negócios. Com investimento de R$ 76 milhões, provenientes do Sebrae Nacional e das unidades estaduais participantes, o equipamento conta com capacidade inicial de armazenamento de 2 petabytes, com possibilidade de expansão futura. Um dos diferenciais da estrutura é o sistema de energia solar instalado especificamente para atender à demanda do data center, com baterias de lítio para armazenamento de energia, reforçando a proposta de aliar infraestrutura tecnológica e eficiência energética. Além do Rio Grande do Norte, serão atendidos os estados do Acre, Amapá, Amazonas, Espírito Santo, Maranhão, Pará, Paraíba, Piauí, Roraima, Sergipe e Tocantins. O Data Center Senador Fernando Bezerra é o segundo do Sistema Sebrae no país. O primeiro foi inaugurado em 2024, no Distrito Federal. Durante a cerimônia de inauguração e descerramento da placa do Data Center Sebrae Senador Fernando Bezerra, representantes do Sebrae Nacional e das unidades estaduais participantes destacaram a importância da estrutura para a segurança da informação, a inovação e o fortalecimento dos pequenos negócios. Tecnologia e novas oportunidades Representando o Sebrae Nacional, o gerente da Unidade de Tecnologia da Informação, Diego Ramos, destacou a importância da inauguração para a instituição e para o desenvolvimento tecnológico do Rio Grande do Norte. Segundo ele, o projeto vai além do investimento em infraestrutura e poderá contribuir para a criação de oportunidades de negócios e o fortalecimento de um ecossistema de inovação no estado. “Esse lançamento marca não somente a história do Sebrae-RN, mas também a do estado. É o primeiro data center verde do Rio Grande do Norte, e isso traz não apenas tecnologia, mas oportunidades de novos negócios”, afirmou. Almeida ressaltou ainda que o equipamento integra a estratégia de criação da Nuvem Sebrae, iniciativa que prevê a interligação de data centers de diferentes estados para ampliar a capacidade tecnológica da instituição e qualificar o atendimento às micro e pequenas empresas diante dos avanços da transformação digital e da inteligência artificial. “Daqui a alguns anos, não vamos estar mais discutindo qual é a capacidade desse data center, mas, sim, a quantidade de histórias e de momentos importantes que ele deixou para tantos micro e pequenos empresários desse Brasil”, concluiu. O vice-presidente da Associação Brasileira dos Sebraes Estaduais (Abase) e diretor-superintendente do Sebrae Paraíba, Luis Alberto Gonçalves de Amorim, também destacou a relevância da iniciativa para acompanhar as transformações tecnológicas e preparar a instituição para os desafios futuros. “A evolução tecnológica exige atualização constante, planejamento e cooperação entre as unidades estaduais. A implantação do equipamento demonstra a importância de unir esforços e investir em soluções capazes de responder às novas demandas da sociedade e dos pequenos negócios”, pontuou. Integração para fortalecer os pequenos negócios O diretor-superintendente do Sebrae-RN, Zeca Melo, enfatizou a importância da integração entre as unidades estaduais e do apoio do Conselho Deliberativo para viabilizar projetos estratégicos da instituição. Ele também reconheceu o trabalho das equipes de Tecnologia da Informação envolvidas na implantação do equipamento. Ao destacar a dimensão do público potencialmente beneficiado, Zeca Melo ressaltou que os 12 estados participantes reúnem milhões de pequenos negócios, o que reforça a importância da atuação conjunta para ampliar a capacidade de atendimento do Sebrae. “Esses 12 estados representam quase 3 milhões de pequenos negócios. A implantação desse data center fortalece a estrutura tecnológica do Sebrae e amplia nossa capacidade de atender aos pequenos negócios, contribuindo para o desenvolvimento e a modernização da instituição em todo o país”, afirmou. Homenagem a Fernando Bezerra A solenidade também marcou a homenagem ao senador Fernando Bezerra, que dá nome ao equipamento. Engenheiro, empresário, ex-presidente da Confederação Nacional da Indústria (CNI), senador da República e ministro, ele teve atuação importante na trajetória do Sebrae-RN. Na década de 1990, foi o primeiro presidente do Conselho Deliberativo Estadual da instituição e contribuiu para viabilizar a aquisição do imóvel onde funciona a atual sede, em Natal. Durante a cerimônia, Fernando Bezerra destacou a contribuição do Sebrae para o desenvolvimento econômico do Brasil e do Rio Grande do Norte. Ele também defendeu maior aproximação entre o poder público, a instituição e as entidades empresariais para impulsionar o crescimento do estado. “O Rio Grande do Norte, se ouvisse mais o Sebrae, estaria muito melhor. A força do desenvolvimento se faz com a iniciativa privada e com iniciativas como a do Sebrae aqui no Rio Grande do Norte”, afirmou. Após o descerramento da placa, os convidados participaram de uma visita guiada às instalações do Data Center Sebrae Senador Fernando Bezerra, que passa a integrar a infraestrutura tecnológica do Sistema Sebrae no país. >> Receba notícias do NOVO em tempo real pelo WhatsApp Receba notícias em primeira mão pelo Whatsapp Assine nosso canal no Telegram Siga o NOVO no Instagram Siga o NOVO no Twitter Acompanhe o NOVO n

artigo.texto: China is giving sodium-ion batteries a temporary tax advantage over conventional lithium-ion technology as manufacturers look to bring the alternative chemistry into commercial electric vehicles. One of the country’s leading sodium-ion battery developers, Hina Battery, is planning a 10 GWh production base in Wuhan and has partnered with a vehicle manufacturer to develop electric sanitation trucks. The expansion comes as China introduces a consumption tax on specified lithium-ion batteries while exempting qualifying sodium-ion batteries through 2028. The policy could improve the economics of sodium-ion production, although falling lithium prices have narrowed the cost gap between the two chemistries. The technology is also attracting attention for its performance in extreme cold. FAW Jiefang reported that one of its electric heavy trucks equipped with a sodium-ion battery retained more than 90% of its usable capacity during testing at minus 40 degrees Fahrenheit. Creating a tax advantage for sodium-ion batteries China’s Ministry of Finance, General Administration of Customs and State Taxation Administration issued Announcement No. 20 (2026) on July 16, revising consumption tax rules for several battery categories. From September 1, 2026, specified lithium-ion batteries became subject to a 2% consumption tax. The rate is scheduled to rise to 4% on September 1, 2027. Qualifying sodium-ion batteries, solid-state batteries and fuel cells are exempt from the tax through December 31, 2028, provided they meet applicable national standards. More from Transportation See All The exemption gives sodium-ion manufacturers a temporary fiscal advantage, but it does not automatically make their products cheaper to produce. Battery-grade lithium carbonate averaged approximately $13,500, per metric ton on October 28. Meanwhile, square lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells for electric vehicles averaged about 5.7 US cents, per watt-hour on October 22. Sodium is more widely distributed geographically than lithium, potentially offering manufacturers a more diversified raw-material supply. However, the downstream sodium-ion supply chain remains concentrated in China, particularly in cell manufacturing, cathode materials and hard-carbon production. Hina targets commercial vehicle production in Wuhan Hina Battery signed an agreement with Wuhan’s Jiangxia District on October 14 to establish a sodium-ion battery production base with planned annual capacity of 10 GWh, with the first phase expected to provide 3 GWh of capacity. Construction is scheduled to begin in early 2027, with initial production targeted before the end of that year. The project was announced during the fourth National Sodium Battery Symposium, showcasing China’s effort to move sodium-ion technology beyond laboratory development and into larger-scale manufacturing. Hina has also signed a separate agreement with Chengli Special Automobile Group to develop sodium-ion-powered sanitation vehicles. The planned lineup includes refuse collection trucks, hook-lift vehicles, dust-suppression trucks and food-waste collection vehicles. Sodium-ion batteries have several potential advantages over lithium-ion alternatives, including access to more widely available raw materials and the possibility of better performance in low temperatures. Their main limitation remains lower energy density, which can translate into heavier or larger battery packs for the same amount of stored energy.

artigo.texto: Share This Article The Connecticut-based company behind a data center planned in Arkansas sued local officials in federal court Thursday over regulations targeting projects like it, claiming the county didn’t have the authority to enact such limits and that the state’s open meetings law was circumvented. The 38-page lawsuit, filed in the U.S. District Court of Eastern Arkansas, accused Pulaski County of enacting regulations targeting AVAIO Digital’s planned data center that infringe on the federal government’s authority to regulate interstate electrical transmission and commerce. AVAIO asked the court for an injunction preventing the regulations from being applied to its project, monetary damages and for the disclosure of public records it said had been withheld from them. It marks the second lawsuit filed in federal court this year connected to data center projects that have appeared in the state over the last two years. Entergy Arkansas unsuccessfully sued the Arkansas Democrat-Gazette, one of its reporters and a local resident in September over the publication of details of the utility’s power agreement for Google’s West Memphis data center that the resident obtained through a public records request. The regulations AVAIO is contesting went into effect earlier this week after the quorum court overrode Democratic Judge Barry Hyde’s veto of them, and were drafted in response to community anger over AVAIO’s project located just off 145th Street. The regulations create uncertainty and threaten AVAIO’s “existing business, financial, and investment arrangements,” the company wrote in the complaint. The lawsuit also accused Democratic nominee for county judge, Wendell Griffen, of having “unlawful control over the Pulaski County Quorum Court,” pointing to his role authoring and advocating for the regulations. Griffen told the Arkansas Advocate that the lawsuit was expected, and said it was the county’s “constitutional power” to regulate data centers within its boundaries. A spokesperson for Pulaski County did not immediately respond to a request for comment Friday evening. The company said Griffen and several members of the quorum court engaged in polling and deliberations that violated the Arkansas Freedom of Information Act. The lawsuit also named Democratic Justice of the Peace Julie Blackwood, who was the lead legislative sponsor of the regulations. Griffen also disputed AVAIO’s characterizations of his communications with quorum court members. “If they contend that a private citizen exercising his First Amendment right to approach members of the legislative body of the county about a matter of public interest is unlawful authority, then they need to reread the First Amendment to the Constitution of the United States,” Griffen said. The ordinance “is without effect because it is an obstacle to the full exercise of the federal government’s authorities under the Federal Power Act to regulate the transmission of electricity,” AVAIO wrote in its complaint. The alleged polling, the company said, also makes the passed ordinance invalid. Judge Lee Rudofsky, who oversaw Entergy’s lawsuit against the Democrat-Gazette, is the assigned judge on the case. artigo.texto: Preparar as condições necessárias para o desenvolvimento de um mercado de carbono florestal. O mercado de carbono florestal abre oportunidades para gerar recursos financeiros para a proteção e o desenvolvimento florestal, ao mesmo tempo que cria demandas por dados, capacidade de gestão e mecanismos de implementação transparentes. Capacitar agências de gestão, empresas e a comunidade com conhecimento é um passo necessário para abordar essa área. Essa informação foi apresentada em uma sessão de treinamento sobre o mercado de carbono florestal, organizada pelo Departamento de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente da cidade de Can Tho, em coordenação com as unidades relevantes, no dia 30 de outubro. Segundo o Sr. Vo Van Tuong, Vice-Chefe do Departamento de Desenvolvimento Rural e Florestal da cidade de Can Tho , as florestas desempenham um papel crucial no meio ambiente e na vida das pessoas. Em particular, os manguezais costeiros contribuem para reduzir o impacto das ondas, proteger diques marítimos, limitar a erosão e criar habitats para muitas espécies animais. No entanto, os esforços de proteção florestal ainda enfrentam muitas dificuldades devido aos impactos das mudanças climáticas, da erosão e dos desafios aos meios de subsistência das pessoas. Segundo o Sr. Tuong, compreender as normas relativas aos serviços de sequestro e armazenamento de carbono prestados pelas florestas é essencial. Além de proteger as áreas florestais existentes, as agências e unidades precisam atualizar regularmente as informações, aprimorar a capacidade profissional e preparar dados para fins de gestão. Isso proporcionará às localidades uma base mais sólida para pesquisa e implementação de atividades que estejam em conformidade com as normas legais e as condições locais. Can Tho possui uma área florestal planejada de aproximadamente 23.195 hectares dentro de seu escopo estatístico, dos quais cerca de 14.500 hectares são florestados. Esses dados são importantes para o monitoramento da situação atual e para o desenvolvimento de planos de gestão, proteção e desenvolvimento florestal no futuro. Durante o programa, a Sra. Tran Thuy Dung, representante do Departamento de Cooperação Internacional do Ministério da Agricultura e do Meio Ambiente, apresentou o roteiro nacional de ação relacionado ao carbono verde. Carbono verde é a quantidade de carbono armazenada em ecossistemas marinhos e costeiros, como manguezais, pradarias marinhas e zonas úmidas costeiras. Esses ecossistemas são de grande importância para o meio ambiente e para a vida das pessoas. Os manguezais contribuem para a proteção do litoral, reduzindo o impacto das ondas e criando habitats para muitas espécies aquáticas. Eles também são um recurso intimamente ligado aos meios de subsistência das pessoas que vivem em áreas costeiras. Você também pode gostar Segundo a Sra. Dung, a pesquisa e o desenvolvimento de projetos relacionados ao carbono verde devem ser baseados em critérios específicos e dados do mundo real. As unidades precisam definir claramente o estado atual da floresta, a extensão da área em consideração, a capacidade de coletar informações e as responsabilidades das partes envolvidas. Esses aspectos formam a base para garantir um processo de avaliação bem fundamentado e evitar conclusões precipitadas, baseadas em informações insuficientes. Uma das questões abordadas é o monitoramento e a verificação dos resultados da implementação do projeto. É necessário coletar informações sobre a área, o estado da floresta e o sequestro de carbono utilizando métodos apropriados, garantindo a verificabilidade e a comparabilidade. Além disso, as partes participantes precisam esclarecer seus direitos de gestão na área, suas responsabilidades pela proteção florestal e os mecanismos de coordenação durante a implementação. A Sra. Dung observou que nem todas as áreas florestais atendem plenamente às condições para a implementação de um projeto de carbono. A avaliação precisa ser baseada em critérios e informações específicas para cada localidade. Para áreas com dados insuficientes, as unidades competentes precisam continuar realizando levantamentos, coletando informações e esclarecendo questões relacionadas antes de tirar quaisquer conclusões . Segundo dados da Parceria para Ação do Carbono Azul no Vietnã (NBCAP Vietnam), a área de manguezal no Delta do Mekong é de aproximadamente 73.200 hectares, representando cerca de 52% da área total de manguezal em todo o país. Desse total, Can Tho possui 5.935 hectares, ocupando o terceiro lugar na região e o quinto lugar em todo o país em termos de área de manguezal. Esse ecossistema desempenha um papel crucial na proteção do ambiente costeiro e no sustento das populações locais. Para a cidade de Can Tho e áreas relacionadas a ecossistemas costeiros, a análise de projetos deve basear-se em levantamentos específicos. Esses levantamentos devem esclarecer o estado atual da floresta, as condições de manejo, as fontes de dados e a capacidade de atender aos requisitos. Essa etapa é necessária para garantir que haja informações suficientes disponíveis antes de se considerar a viabilidade da implementação do projeto. O Sr. Vu Tan Phuong, Diretor do Centro de Certificação de Gestão Florestal do Vietnã (VFCC), acredita que, para desenvolver o mercado de créditos de carbono florestal, é necessário sincronizar políticas e normas técnicas, além de aprimorar a capacidade de implementação das partes interessadas. Segundo o Sr. Vu Tan Phuong, órgãos de gestão florestal, proprietários de florestas e empresas precisam estar munidos de conhecimento sobre inventários de gases de efeito estufa, cálculo de carbono, desenvolvimento e gestão de projetos, bem como sobre o processo de avaliação, verificação e emissão de créditos de carbono. Além disso, é necessário aprimorar as diretrizes e construir um banco de dados para apoiar o monitoramento, o relato e a avaliação do potencial de carbono florestal. artigo.texto: Storing electricity at the scale of several gigawatt-hours is becoming a reality for power grids around the world. From a solar-powered development in Abu Dhabi to battery installations across Saudi Arabia, these projects are designed to store electricity and supply it when it is needed. The following list includes individual facilities, multi-site programs, and phased developments, with capacities reflecting their published scope. Some are already operating, others remain under development, and Moss Landing illustrates why historical capacity must be distinguished from what a facility can deliver today. 1. Masdar–EWEC round-the-clock project, UAE -19 GWh Abu Dhabi’s Masdar–EWEC development combines a 5.2-gigawatt solar plant with 19 gigawatt-hours of battery storage. The project is designed to deliver 1 gigawatt of renewable electricity around the clock, extending solar power delivery beyond daylight hours. Masdar laid the foundation for the project in October 2025, with operations targeted for 2027. Its design includes grid-forming technology, black-start capability, and forecasting and dispatch systems to coordinate electricity generation, storage, and delivery. 2. SEC–BYD battery storage program, Saudi Arabia – 12.5 GWh BYD announced a 12.5-gigawatt-hour energy storage contract with Saudi Electricity Company in February 2025. The agreement covers multiple grid-scale projects and brings BYD’s combined Saudi cooperation with the utility to 15.1 gigawatt-hours, including an earlier 2.6-gigawatt-hour delivery. More from Energy See All MEED identifies the program as five facilities with a combined power rating of 2.5 gigawatts, built with Alfanar as the engineering, procurement, and construction contractor. Equipment supplier NR Electric reported that SEC’s five-region, 2.5-gigawatt storage project completed its grid-connected charging and discharging tests on May 27, 2026, marking commissioning. 3. Oasis de Atacama, Chile – 14.1 GWh (overall platform) Grenergy’s Oasis de Atacama is a phased solar and battery storage development in Chile. Although earlier plans set its storage capacity at about 11 gigawatt-hours, the company’s September 2026 announcement raised the overall platform a capacity to 14.1 gigawatt-hours. That figure reflects the wider development, with individual phases coming online separately. Grenergy confirmed in September 2026 that Gabriela, the fourth phase, was operational with 272 megawatts of solar generation and 1,100 megawatt-hours of battery storage. 4. Najran, Khamis Mushait, and Madaya storage program, Saudi Arabia – 7.8 GWh Saudi Arabia’s 7.8-gigawatt-hour storage deployment spans three sites at Najran, Khamis Mushait, and Madaya. Sungrow supplied more than 1,500 PowerTitan 2.0 systems and announced grid connection completion in December 2025. The equipment integrates batteries, power conversion systems, medium-voltage transformers, and switching equipment into preassembled units. Sungrow says factory testing and preassembly reduced on-site installation work, while a local service team supported installation, commissioning, and grid connection. 5. Envision Jingyi Chagan Hada, China – 4 GWh The Envision Jingyi Chagan Hada Energy Storage Power Station in Inner Mongolia has a reported capacity of 4 gigawatt-hours. It connected to the grid in late December 2025, forming part of Envision’s wider 12.8-gigawatt-hour regional storage cluster. According to the Sustainable Markets Initiative’s project showcase, the station passed the grid’s three-charge, three-discharge verification in a single attempt. Its control system combines forecasting, dispatch, and electricity-market trading, coordinating how stored energy is managed and sold. 6. Edwards & Sanborn, USA – 3.287 GWh California’s Edwards & Sanborn project combines solar generation with 3.287 gigawatt-hours of battery storage. Developer Terra-Gen and contractor Mortenson announced substantial completion of the Kern County development in January 2024. The installation spans more than 4,600 acres, with part of the project on Edwards Air Force Base. Mortenson identifies LG Chem, Samsung, and BYD as battery suppliers, while the project serves customers including California utilities, the city of San Jose, and Starbucks. 7. Moss Landing, USA – 3 GWh (historical installed capacity) Vistra’s Moss Landing Energy Storage Facility reached 750 megawatts and 3,000 megawatt-hours of installed capacity after its third expansion entered commercial operation in June 2023. That expansion added 350 megawatts and 1,400 megawatt-hours, establishing the California site as a major early example of multi-gigawatt-hour battery storage. Its historical capacity requires qualification following the January 2025 fire at the 300-megawatt facility. EPA confirms that the affected building has had no active battery storage operations since that incident, while Vistra subsequently decided not to return the separate 100-megawatt facility to service. 8. Collie Battery, Australia – 2.24 GWh Neoen’s Collie Battery in Western Australia has a combined capacity of 560 megawatts and 2,240 megawatt-hours. The development comprises a 219-megawatt first stage and a 341-megawatt second stage; the company’s October 2025 update said both are operational. The service addresses electricity reliability risks associated with coal-plant retirements, growing rooftop solar generation, and demand on Western Australia’s South-West Interconnected System. 9. Bisha BESS, Saudi Arabia – 2 GWh The Bisha battery storage facility in Saudi Arabia’s Aseer province is rated at 500 megawatts and 2,000 megawatt-hours. Contractor Alfanar describes the delivered installation as a four-hour system that stores electricity during low-demand periods for redistribution when demand rises. Bisha has also demonstrated a capability needed after a major grid outage: black start, or restoring power without relying on an already energized network. artigo.texto: Prepare the necessary conditions for the development of a forest carbon market. The forest carbon market opens up opportunities to generate financial resources for forest protection and development, while also creating demands for data, management capacity, and transparent implementation mechanisms. Equipping management agencies, businesses, and the community with knowledge is a necessary step in approaching this field. This information was presented at a training session on the forest carbon market organized by the Department of Agriculture and Environment of Can Tho City in coordination with relevant units on October 30th. According to Mr. Vo Van Tuong, Deputy Head of the Rural Development and Forestry Department of Can Tho City , forests play a crucial role in the environment and people's lives. In particular, coastal mangrove forests contribute to reducing the impact of waves, protecting sea dikes, limiting erosion, and creating habitats for many animal species. However, forest protection efforts still face many difficulties due to the impacts of climate change, erosion, and challenges to people's livelihoods. According to Mr. Tuong, understanding the regulations on carbon sequestration and storage services provided by forests is essential. Besides protecting existing forest areas, agencies and units need to regularly update information, improve professional capacity, and prepare data for management purposes. This will provide localities with a stronger basis for research and implementation of activities that comply with legal regulations and local conditions. Can Tho has a planned forestry land area of approximately 23,195 hectares within its statistical scope, of which about 14,500 hectares are forested. These are important figures for monitoring the current status and developing plans for forest management, protection, and development in the future. At the program, Ms. Tran Thuy Dung, representative of the International Cooperation Department, Ministry of Agriculture and Environment, presented the national action roadmap related to green carbon. Green carbon is the amount of carbon stored in marine and coastal ecosystems, such as mangrove forests, seagrass beds, and coastal wetlands. These ecosystems are of great importance to the environment and the lives of the people. Mangrove forests contribute to protecting coastlines, reducing the impact of waves, and creating habitats for many aquatic species. They are also a resource closely linked to the livelihoods of people in coastal areas. Units need to clearly define the current state of the forest, the scope of the area under consideration, the ability to collect information, and the responsibilities of the relevant parties. These aspects form the basis for ensuring a well-founded assessment process and avoiding conclusions drawn without sufficient information. One of the issues addressed is the monitoring and verification of project implementation results. Information on area, forest status, and carbon sequestration needs to be collected using appropriate methods, ensuring verifiability and comparability. Furthermore, participating parties need to clarify their management rights in the area, responsibilities for forest protection, and coordination mechanisms during implementation. Ms. Dung noted that not all forested areas fully meet the conditions for implementing a carbon project. The assessment needs to be based on specific criteria and information for each locality. For areas lacking sufficient data, relevant units need to continue surveying, gathering information, and clarifying related issues before making any conclusions . According to data from the Blue Carbon Action Partnership in Vietnam (NBCAP Vietnam), the mangrove forest area in the Mekong Delta is approximately 73,200 hectares, accounting for about 52% of the total mangrove forest area nationwide. Of this, Can Tho has 5,935 hectares, ranking third in the region and fifth nationwide in terms of mangrove forest area. This ecosystem plays a crucial role in protecting the coastal environment and supporting the livelihoods of local people. For Can Tho city and areas related to coastal ecosystems, project consideration should be based on specific surveys. These surveys should clarify the current state of the forest, management conditions, data sources, and the ability to meet the requirements. This is a necessary step to ensure sufficient information is available before considering the feasibility of project implementation. Mr. Vu Tan Phuong, Director of the Vietnam Forest Management Certification Center (VFCC), believes that to develop the forest carbon credit market, it is necessary to synchronize policies, technical standards, and enhance the implementation capacity of relevant stakeholders. According to Mr. Vu Tan Phuong, management agencies, forest owners, and businesses need to be equipped with knowledge about greenhouse gas inventories, carbon calculation, project development and management, as well as the process of appraisal, verification, and issuance of carbon credits. Furthermore, it is necessary to refine guidelines and build a database to support the monitoring, reporting, and assessment of forest carbon potential. The selection of priority areas, investment attraction, and project implementation must comply with legal regulations, meet applicable standards, ensure transparency, and avoid duplication in recording emission reduction results. During the training session, participants were also introduced to the basics of the carbon market and regulations related to the forestry sector. The carbon market can be understood as a mechanism that allows trading of emission reduction results or carbon storage amounts when certain conditions are met. artigo.texto: MELBOURNE, Australia, Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On October 28, HiTHIUM, a leading global energy storage technology company, showcased its ∞Power 6.9MWh 8-hour long-duration battery energy storage system (BESS) at All Energy Australia in Melbourne, alongside its grid compliance capabilities, localized service network and energy storage solutions for C&I and residential applications. Long-duration energy storage is increasingly important for grid flexibility and supply reliability in Australia. The federal government supports dispatchable clean energy projects through the Capacity Investment Scheme (CIS), while New South Wales continues to advance dedicated LDES tenders, creating new opportunities for storage projects of eight hours or longer. At the exhibition, HiTHIUM showcased its ∞Power 6.9MWh 8-hour-native BESS. Australia's high-price events are lengthening, with 4-hour-plus events accounting for over 70% of scarcity revenue in 2025 and shifting storage value toward firm supply duration. CSIRO GenCost analysis shows that two 4-hour systems delivering the same 8-hour output would cost about 23% more than a purpose-built 8-hour system, which offers greater value potential during price peaks. Integrated into a standard 20-foot container, ∞Power 6.9MWh BESS offers up to 96% round-trip efficiency, a 25-year design life, and compatibility with PCS and EMS products from major global suppliers. Compared with a 4-hour configuration, it reduces land use by 15% and can lower LCOS through system optimization. Developed in line with NFPA, IEC and AS standards, the system also delivers a high level of safety. To address Australia's grid connection requirements, HiTHIUM presented its Grid Compliance Simulation and Verification Platform, supporting projects through grid connection, from R0 assessment and R1 capability assessment to commissioning and R2 model validation. By combining grid-code interpretation, plant-level modelling, automated simulation, hardware-in-the-loop testing and site measurement validation, the platform helps identify potential compliance risks earlier and reduce late-stage rework. HiTHIUM continues to strengthen its localized service capabilities in Australia. The company has established a localized service network across Australia, covering spare-parts warehousing, training, operations and maintenance (O&M), and compliant battery recycling, with nationwide service coverage. At the exhibition, HiTHIUM signed strategic cooperation agreements with Raystech, Ingeteam and other Australian partners to further strengthen its local workforce, spare-parts infrastructure and safety capabilities. The company also announced that its Brisbane service center is scheduled to open by mid-2027, further expanding its regional service network and bringing efficient, reliable support closer to Australian customers. HiTHIUM also showcased its ∞Power 1022kWh liquid-cooled C&I energy storage cabinet, which combines its proprietary ∞Cell 1175Ah LDES cells with an integrated design for applications including peak shaving and solar self-consumption. For residential applications, the company presented the HeroEE 16 and ARKVOLT F8S series, supporting flexible deployment and integration with solar, heat pumps and EV charging. Through its 8-hour LDES technology, grid compliance expertise and expanding local service network, HiTHIUM is strengthening its ability to support Australian energy storage projects from development and grid connection through long-term operation. These efforts reflect HiTHIUM's commitment to supporting Australia's evolving energy storage needs with integrated solutions and sustained local support.

artigo.texto: Politics & Government Dixon May Extend Data Center, Battery Storage Ban: Report City officials want more time to study potential impacts on water, electricity and surrounding neighborhoods. DIXON, CA — Dixon officials are considering extending a temporary ban on new data centers and battery energy storage facilities through September 2027 as the city develops regulations for the projects, according to The Independent Voice. The City Council will consider extending the existing 45-day moratorium for another 10 months and 15 days at its Tuesday meeting, the newspaper reported. The city adopted the temporary restrictions in late September to evaluate how the facilities could affect water supplies, electricity demand, noise levels and emissions. The city's municipal code does not specifically identify data centers or battery energy storage systems as permitted uses. Without dedicated standards, officials would need to determine whether proposed facilities fit within existing land-use categories. Data centers house computer equipment used to process and store digital information, while battery energy storage systems store electricity for later use. artigo.texto: Indonesia’s SM+ Data Centers and LG Sinar Mas, together with Korea Investment Real Asset Management (KIRA), have today opened a 21-megawatt (MW) AI-ready data center in Jakarta, the firms’ joint press release said. The facility, known as SMX01, is ready for service with customer onboarding and stabilizing operations being priorities now. The colocation facility has attracted interest from prospective global, regional, and domestic customers. Located in Jakarta’s central business district, SMX01 is designed to accommodate conventional enterprise workloads and higher-density AI computing, with flexibility for modular expansion as demand increases. The facility is owned and managed by SM+ Data Centers, with KIRA as the investment partner and LG Sinar Mas, a joint venture between South Korea’s LG CNS and Sinar Mas-backed SM+, in charge of its design, construction, and technical operations. “Computing requirements are becoming more varied. Some still run conventional systems, while others are beginning to need significantly higher performance capacity for AI. That is why we built SMX01 so it can expand alongside the market and our customers’ needs,” said Herson Suindah, President Director and Group CEO of SM+ Holdings. “SMX01 reaching Ready for Service is an important investment milestone because it turns long-term capital into operating digital infrastructure that can support Indonesia’s next phase of digital growth. We see strong fundamentals in the market, and we are pleased to continue working with SM+ Data Centers and LG Sinar Mas as the facility moves from development into operations,” said Yong Sik Kim, CEO of KIRA. “A data center’s readiness for AI cannot be measured by rack numbers alone. Power, cooling, and structural load capacity must be planned together from the outset. This is the approach we have brought from our experience building and operating data centers in Korea and globally,” said Donghyup Han, CEO of LG Sinar Mas. SM+ owns and manages 31 data centers across 25 Indonesian cities, including 30 edge data centers, with nearly 45 MW of combined IT load capacity in operations.

artigo.texto: O alcance da medida atinge setores estratégicos da economia nacional, como ferro, aço, alumínio, cimento, fertilizantes e hidrogênio. Por Ana Paula Oriola De Raeffray e Louis Henri Frederic De Raeffray A precificação de carbono deixou definitivamente o campo dos discursos ambientais para se consolidar como variável bruta de comércio exterior, competitividade e acesso ao mercado europeu. Com a entrada em sua fase definitiva, o Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) da União Europeia impõe uma nova realidade: o teor de emissões incorporado aos bens exportados determina, agora, o seu custo efetivo de entrada no bloco. O alcance da medida atinge diretamente setores estratégicos da economia nacional, como ferro, aço, alumínio, cimento, fertilizantes e hidrogênio. Para além do valor nominal dos certificados vinculados ao mercado europeu (EU ETS), o ponto cego para o exportador brasileiro reside na assimetria de mensuração. Duas toneladas de aço fisicamente idênticas enfrentarão condições econômicas totalmente distintas na aduana europeia, a depender do volume de emissões do processo produtivo, das metodologias de comprovação e do aproveitamento do preço de carbono pago no país de origem. É justamente nesse gargalo que o Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissões (SBCE), instituído pela Lei nº 15.042/2024, ganha dimensão comercial crítica. A consulta pública lançada pelo Ministério da Fazenda em julho de 2026 — introduzindo gradualmente as regras de Monitoramento, Relato e Verificação (MRV) para indústrias de base — expôs a urgência desse alinhamento. A legislação europeia permite deduzir do encargo do CBAM os valores efetivamente quitados no Brasil, mas essa compensação exige equivalência metodológica e validação documental aceitas em Bruxelas. Sem a célere garantia de interoperabilidade entre as métricas brasileiras e as exigências europeias, o risco de dupla oneração econômica torna-se iminente. A indústria nacional corre o perigo real de arcar com o custo doméstico de carbono sem conseguir abatê-lo nas exportações para a Europa, perdendo margem e competitividade perante players globais. A gravidade do tema já extrapolou a esfera regulatória interna e atingiu o contencioso comercial internacional. Não por acaso, em setembro de 2026, o Órgão de Solução de Controvérsias da Organização Mundial do Comércio (OMC) acolheu a criação de um painel para analisar a conformidade do CBAM e do EU ETS. A presença do Brasil como terceiro interessado — ao lado de potências como China, Índia, Estados Unidos e Japão — ratifica que a suposta neutralidade comercial do mecanismo europeu é alvo de forte questionamento global. Para a indústria de transformação no Brasil, a discussão deixou de ser conceitual e passou a ser estritamente operacional. Não basta acompanhar a cotação das licenças de carbono; exige-se mapear precursores, mensurar emissões incorporadas com rigor auditável e transmitir dados incontestáveis aos importadores. O debate migrou da sustentabilidade isolada para a mesa da diretoria financeira, do compliance e do planejamento de vendas. Paralelamente, o avanço do CBAM reconfigura a segurança jurídica da contratação internacional. Cláusulas de fornecimento antes restritas a alíquotas aduaneiras e Incoterms exigem, a partir de agora, regramento explícito sobre a alocação do risco tributário do carbono, deveres de transparência nas emissões e garantias de auditoria. A capacidade de estruturar contratos juridicamente blindados contra contenciosos internacionais — seja em arbitragens de comércio exterior ou perante cortes estrangeiras — tornou-se pilar tão decisivo quanto a eficiência operacional da fábrica. O Brasil encontra-se diante de um divisor de águas. O país detém uma das matrizes energéticas mais limpas do planeta, mas arrisca perder mercados globais por falhas de integração institucional. Não cabe ao Estado ou ao setor produtivo adotar uma postura passiva. É fundamental acelerar a regulamentação do SBCE com foco na diplomacia comercial, enquanto as lideranças empresariais devem encarar a contabilidade de carbono como investimento prioritário em inteligência de mercado. Em suma, o carbono passou a compor o preço final do produto ao lado do frete, do câmbio e das tarifas alfandegárias. Para os exportadores brasileiros, a adaptação soberana e rigorosa a essas exigências não representa um debate para o futuro: é a condição imediata para a sobrevivência comercial no cenário global. (Ana Paula Oriola De Raeffray é doutora em Direito pela Pontifícia Universidade Católica de São Paulo (PUC-SP) e Louis Henri Frederic De Raeffray é consultor do escritório Raeffray Brugioni Advogados) PARTICIPAÇÃO DO LEITOR Participe desta discussão Compartilhe sua opinião sobre este assunto. artigo.texto: Via a brief news release on Oct. 26, Anthropic said that it had filed a registration statement on Form S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) regarding its upcoming initial public offering (IPO). There's not much detail on the release, but the prospectus with the SEC shows that the San Francisco-based company that developed the AI chatbot Claude sees a five-year power bottleneck. The company is moving from a cloud-only, fixed-time compute model to a hybrid setup that includes directly leased chips hosted in data center facilities. In the prospectus, Anthropic discusses launching a new initiative, "Anthropic Direct," to build its own dedicated data centers rather than relying entirely on third-party cloud providers. The company expects this move to lower its long-term costs. Partner companies will buy the land, secure power, build the facilities, and run the daily operations. Anthropic will then lease the computing power directly from those partners. Last month, Anthropic began signing these agreements, committing to $125.2 billion in lease payments over five years, before interest. Anthropic is likely to use behind-the-meter power generation for its data centers to accelerate its development. How Bloom Energy could benefit Bloom Energy (BE -8.61%) provides an alternative to drawing power from a centralized electrical grid through on-site solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) technology. The energy company's SOFCs provide continuous low-emission electrical power. Instead of waiting for a power grid to ramp up to power an Anthropic data center, Anthropic can use Bloom Energy's modular generators to bring data centers online sooner. It isn't far-fetched that Anthropic would turn to Bloom because several of Anthropic cloud-based partners already use Bloom for power needs. Amazon (AMZN -1.41%), through Amazon Web Services, is a major cloud partner for Anthropic. AWS works closely with American Electric Power (AEP +0.67%), which deploys Bloom Energy fuel cells across multiple data center campuses. Specialized cloud provider CoreWeave (CRWV -9.66%), which works with Anthropic, has a partnership to use Bloom Energy power cells at a data center. Bloom is already seeing strong growth The company's financial strength and growing stability are two other reasons Anthropic would turn to it rather than another power provider. Bloom Energy posted record numbers in the third quarter. It reported revenue of $1.26 billion, up 138% year over year. That allowed the company to raise full-year revenue guidance to between $4.4 billion and $4.6 billion, up 122% at the midpoint. BE Bloom Energy NYSE · As of 5:00 PM ET 10/30/26 It's not just revenue that's growing. The company reported earnings per share (EPS) of $0.78, up from an EPS loss of $0.10 in the same period a year ago. Bloom points to a yearly non-GAAP (generally accepted accounting principles) EPS range of $3.10 to $3.40, compared to $0.76 in 2025. Bloom has an edge over Oklo Another possibility for Anthropic is to use small modular reactors (SMRs) from Oklo (OKLO -5.82%) to provide behind-the-meter power to its data centers. However, Bloom's SOFCs are already operating at scale. Its systems can be made, delivered, and put into use within months to a year, providing a quick power solution for new data centers. Oklo's SMRs are promising, but its first commercial reactor is not scheduled to come online until 2027 or later, with large-scale multi-gigawatt rollouts pushed out toward 2030 and beyond. On top of that, the regulatory climate for Bloom's power cells is much easier than for any type of nuclear reactor.

artigo.texto: SENER Extends Battery Storage Call Deadline to March 2027 Electricity availability has become one of the key factors determining the feasibility of new industrial investments in Mexico. Against a backdrop of supply chain relocation, manufacturing expansion, and growth in technology-driven industries, securing a reliable power supply represents a challenge that extends well beyond the energy sector. In other news, SENER has officially extended the deadline for energy storage developers to register projects under its strategic generation and storage call to March 1, 2027. This fourth adjustment to the regulatory roadmap provides private sector participants with crucial operational runway to refine technical proposals, optimize project financing structures, and synchronize deployment timelines with CFE. Ready for more? This is your Weekly RoundUp! Power Shortages Threaten Investment in Mexico According to research published in May 2025 by the Mexican Institute for Competitiveness (IMCO), national electricity demand could increase by 13.4% by 2030 compared to 2024 levels. The organization warns that without timely investment, Mexico could face an electricity generation shortfall exceeding 48,000 gigawatt-hours by the end of the decade. CFE Drives New Electricity Expansion in Mexico The modernization of Mexico’s electricity system is entering a new phase of strategic infrastructure investment. CFE presented its 2026-2030 Expansion Plan to industry representatives, outlining 32 electricity transmission projects and four generation initiatives expected to be awarded in the coming months. The presentation took place on October 23 during the company's second Roadshow, with details publicly released on October 27. IRENA 2026 Outlook Calls for Grid, Storage Modernization While global renewable power capacity expansion continues to reach historic records, implementation velocity remains insufficient to align with global climate pathways, reports the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA). In the World Energy Transitions Outlook 2026, IRENA reports that electricity’s share of global final energy consumption must increase from 23% to 35% by 2035 and exceed 50% by 2050, requiring cumulative global investments of US$256 trillion between 2026 and 2050. Achieving these metrics depends on the concurrent expansion of renewable generation, electrical grid infrastructure, utility-scale energy storage, and system flexibility mechanisms. PEMEX Joins Tabasco State Government’s 2026 Reforestation Days The joint initiative aligns with wider efforts to align industrial operations with environmental stewardship and sustainable land use in oil-producing regions. During a previous presentation on company operations, Víctor Rodríguez, CEO, PEMEX, highlighted the company's long-term environmental and operational vision, describing it as a comprehensive vision that strengthens energy sovereignty, improves efficiency, and leverages existing assets, while contributing to sustainability through a gradual reduction of the carbon footprint. Mexico Extends Battery Storage Registration Deadline to March Mexico’s Ministry of Energy (SENER) has officially extended the deadline for energy storage developers to register projects under its strategic generation and storage call to March 1, 2027. Announced through an administrative amendment signed by Minister of Energy Luz Elena González, this fourth adjustment to the regulatory roadmap provides private sector participants with crucial operational runway to refine technical proposals, optimize project financing structures, and synchronize deployment timelines with the state utility CFE.

artigo.texto: Veja o resumo da notícia Uma empresa ligada ao bilionário Elon Musk estaria oferecendo cerca de US$ 180 mil para comprar casas próximas a uma instalação de geração de energia que abastece data centers de inteligência artificial na região de Memphis, nos Estados Unidos. Segundo reportagem do jornal britânico The Guardian, as propostas incluem uma condição: os proprietários que aceitarem vender seus imóveis deverão renunciar ao direito de processar a companhia por transtornos associados à usina. A iniciativa ocorre após reclamações de moradores sobre o barulho constante das turbinas utilizadas para gerar eletricidade e possíveis impactos na qualidade do ar. A estrutura está ligada às operações da SpaceXSI, companhia resultante da incorporação da xAI pela SpaceX, conforme as informações divulgadas. Até o momento, a empresa não se pronunciou publicamente sobre as supostas ofertas de compra. Empresa de Musk pretende comprar mais de 400 casas De acordo com o The Guardian, corretores imobiliários começaram a procurar moradores da região de Southaven, próxima a Memphis, para apresentar propostas de aquisição de residências. Um dos profissionais teria informado a um proprietário que a companhia pretende comprar 418 imóveis, dos quais 18 já teriam acordos fechados. Outras cinco propriedades teriam sido adquiridas pela MZX, empresa responsável pela operação da infraestrutura energética e vinculada à SpaceX. As ofertas giram em torno de US$ 180 mil por residência, valor próximo ao preço médio dos imóveis da região, segundo a reportagem. A intenção seria utilizar as casas adquiridas para acomodar trabalhadores da companhia. Entretanto, a exigência de renúncia a futuras ações judiciais chama a atenção diante das reclamações relacionadas à instalação. Data center utiliza 69 turbinas movidas a gás A expansão da infraestrutura de inteligência artificial de Elon Musk começou com a criação da xAI, em 2023. A empresa desenvolveu o Grok, sistema de inteligência artificial que depende de grande capacidade computacional para funcionar. Em 2024, a xAI começou a instalar data centers na região de Memphis, ampliando a demanda por eletricidade. Para atender às necessidades energéticas dessas operações, a companhia montou uma estrutura de geração em Southaven, composta por 69 turbinas provisórias movidas a gás. O funcionamento dos equipamentos passou a provocar reclamações de moradores das proximidades. Segundo os relatos reunidos pelo jornal, o ruído produzido pela instalação é constante e, em determinados momentos, semelhante ao de uma aeronave. Além da poluição sonora, residentes também demonstraram preocupação com possíveis impactos ambientais associados à operação das turbinas. Moradores entraram com ação coletiva contra empresa As reclamações levaram moradores a recorrer à Justiça em junho de 2026, quando apresentaram uma ação coletiva contra a companhia. O processo questiona os transtornos relacionados ao funcionamento da estrutura energética, principalmente o barulho produzido pelas turbinas. Nesse contexto, a compra das residências poderia reduzir a quantidade de moradores com potencial interesse em apresentar novas reclamações judiciais. No entanto, essa interpretação não comprova que impedir novos processos seja a finalidade principal das aquisições. A reportagem do The Guardian aponta que a exigência de renúncia ao direito de processar a empresa faz parte das condições apresentadas aos proprietários. Empresa promete reduzir barulho das turbinas Em julho, reguladores estaduais e a companhia chegaram a um acordo para transformar a instalação provisória em uma unidade permanente de geração de energia a gás. A expectativa é que a modernização da estrutura reduza os níveis de ruído registrados atualmente. A empresa também havia mencionado outras medidas para diminuir os transtornos, incluindo a instalação de barreiras acústicas e ajustes na potência dos equipamentos. Apesar dessas iniciativas, as supostas ofertas de compra levantam questionamentos sobre a estratégia adotada para lidar com as reclamações da comunidade. A expansão dos data centers destinados à inteligência artificial exige grandes volumes de energia, o que amplia os desafios relacionados à infraestrutura elétrica e aos impactos sobre as regiões onde essas instalações operam. No caso de Southaven, a controvérsia envolve tanto as condições de funcionamento da usina quanto os direitos dos moradores que vivem próximos à estrutura. Meta-descrição: Empresa ligada a Elon Musk oferece US$ 180 mil por casas próximas a data center nos EUA, segundo o The Guardian. Propostas incluem renúncia a processos.

artigo.texto: As the global race to secure electric vehicle (EV) supply chains intensifies, Morocco is positioning itself as a manufacturing hub linking Europe’s automotive market with Asia’s battery industry. Morocco’s emergence as a battery manufacturing hub could create new opportunities for lithium miners, developers, and explorers as the country positions itself to supply Europe’s EV market. Chinese companies are investing US$6 billion ($8.5 billion) in Morocco’s battery supply chain, as previously reported. The investment targets battery cell and cathode material production as manufacturers seek to diversify their operations amid changing trade dynamics between China and the European Union (EU). With the EU imposing additional duties on Chinese-made EVs, manufacturers are looking at production locations that offer access to international markets while reducing exposure to trade restrictions. An established automotive industry Morocco’s push into battery manufacturing builds on an established automotive export industry. The country is Africa’s largest vehicle manufacturing and export hub, generating MAD 93.7 billion ($13.5 billion) in exports by mid-2026. The country is now gaining a greater share of the EV supply chain through the latest investment by Chinese companies. The investment also signals the growing opportunities for the broader mining sector, as the expansion of battery manufacturing capacity increases the importance of securing reliable supplies of lithium for the energy transition. For lithium producers, the Morocco investment could provide an additional source of demand as battery manufacturing capacity expands beyond established production centres in China. However, the lithium sourcing arrangements for the planned facilities have not been disclosed, leaving uncertainty over which producers could benefit and how much additional demand the projects could generate. Developers: Global Lithium For developers and explorers, the expansion of battery manufacturing offers a potential opportunity for projects seeking a place in the evolving global supply chain. As Morocco expands its downstream manufacturing capacity, projects that can show competitive production costs, reliable supply, and a clear pathway to production could position themselves to attract potential customers and strategic partners. Global Lithium Resources (ASX:GL1) is focused on derisking its Manna Lithium Project in Western Australia, ahead of a final investment decision expected by the end of 2026. Manna boasts a 51.6 million tonne (Mt) mineral resource base, which is considered the third-largest in the Kalgoorlie lithium province. An optimised Definitive Feasibility Study (DFS) for the project has been completed, confirming Manna has a long mine life and is an economically robust lithium asset. Developers such as Global Lithium are demonstrating their projects’ economic viability, particularly as new production capacity enters the market. Explorers: Venari Minerals Meanwhile, for explorers, the latest investment in Morocco presents a potential longer-term demand signal rather than an immediate commercial opportunity. Increased battery manufacturing capacity could support the investment case for new lithium discoveries. However, explorers will still need to establish commercially viable resources before they can benefit from any additional demand. For example, Venari Minerals (ASX:VMS) is advancing its Red Mountain Lithium Project in Nevada, US, which hosts a resource of 500Mt @ 0.61% lithium carbonate equivalent. The company recently announced it is seeking US Department of War (DoW) funding for Red Mountain. This follows its admission to the US Defense Industrial Base Consortium. Membership provides access to DoW grant opportunities and a network of defence contractors to support domestic strategic mineral supply chains. It also enables faster collaboration between government, industry, academia, and non-traditional suppliers. Venari has advanced metallurgical test work at the project, with Scoping Study-level leachability results showing that the lithium is highly leachable. Beneficiation test work also revealed that mineralisation has ‘excellent’ characteristics for removing gangue minerals while retaining valuable lithium-bearing clays and reducing acid consumption. The extent to which Morocco’s expansion translates into opportunities for explorers depends on various factors. These include whether manufacturers seek to secure future supply through partnerships, project investments, or offtake agreements. Morocco’s ambitions could create another source of demand for lithium across the supply chain. However, the impact on individual companies will depend on the scale of additional consumption, the origin of raw materials, and how quickly Morocco’s planned battery manufacturing capacity moves into production. Write to Aaliyah Rogan at Mining.com.au Main image: Mining.com.au

artigo.texto: With maritime transport now included in the UK Emissions Trading Scheme, ship managers need to understand how the new requirements sit alongside the EU ETS, what this means for SHIPMAN agreements and where potential debt and liability exposures may arise. Since 1st July 2026, maritime transport has been included in the UK Emissions Trading Scheme (UK ETS). Ship managers must now deal with a second emissions trading scheme to consider alongside the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS). The schemes use separate allowances and have different geographical scopes, but the work involved will be familiar to managers already dealing with the EU ETS. Both schemes require emissions to be monitored, reported and verified, followed by the surrender of allowances. The EU ETS covers voyages between EU and EEA ports, part of voyages between EU and non-EU ports, and emissions in EU ports. The UK ETS initially covers domestic UK voyages and emissions in UK ports. Managers will therefore need to identify the emissions falling under each scheme and ensure the correct allowances are surrendered. Does this mean SHIPMAN must be amended again? In most cases, no. The BIMCO ETS clause in SHIPMAN 2024 was not drafted solely for the EU ETS. An Emission Scheme is defined to include the EU ETS and any similar system imposed by an applicable lawful authority. The wording allows the clause to apply to similar schemes introduced elsewhere, including in the UK, the US or China. Where the BIMCO clause has been used without amendments which narrow its scope, the UK ETS should already be covered. Managers should, however, check any bespoke wording. A clause which refers only to the EU ETS or EU Allowances may not extend to the UK scheme. For managers, a more immediate concern may be whether the owner provides the allowances. Where the manager is the responsible entity under SHIPMAN, the owner must provide the allowances needed for compliance. If the owner fails to transfer them, or the manager purchases allowances and is not reimbursed, a substantial debt may arise. ITIC’s new ship managers’ debt collection cover is relevant in this situation. ITIC can fund approved costs incurred in pursuing unpaid management fees and debts relating to emissions liabilities, including EU ETS and FuelEU liabilities. The cover does not insure the credit risk or pay the cost of the allowances. It covers the costs of recovering money due to the manager. In many cases, an initial approach from ITIC may be sufficient to obtain payment. Where it is not, further recovery action can be considered, such as the appointment of lawyers. A manager may also face a claim arising from an error in carrying out its responsibilities. For example, the manager could submit inaccurate emissions data, allocate emissions to the wrong scheme, fail to report within the required period or surrender the incorrect number of allowances. If an error causes the owner a loss and results in a claim against the manager, ITIC’s professional indemnity cover may respond, subject to terms and conditions of the cover. The distinction between these two exposures is clear. If the owner has failed to pay an amount due, it is a debt recovery issue. If the manager has made an error which causes a loss, it may result in a professional indemnity claim. For managers using the BIMCO ETS clause in SHIPMAN 2024, the arrival of the UK ETS should not in itself mean revisiting the contract. The priority is to check that the clause has not been narrowed through bespoke amendments and that responsibility for providing allowances and reimbursing costs is clear. If the owner does not pay, ITIC may be able to assist with the cost of recovery.

artigo.texto: Data centers are deeply unpopular. But what if we called them something else? Axios reports that OpenAI is preparing a “PR blitz” for after the midterm elections on Tuesday, as Democrats seem likely to win back the House of Representatives, and possibly the Senate, too. The company’s chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane told Axios that the midterms will be “a bit of a movie trailer for what you’re going to see in 2028,” when he expects AI to be “the issue” in the presidential election. artigo.texto: The American Water Works Association (AWWA), an international, nonprofit scientific and educational society, has released a report outlining how water utilities can assess the potential effects of proposed data center developments on water supplies, infrastructure and wastewater systems. The report titled Cooling the Cloud: Considerations for Water Utilities Evaluating Data Center Development, was developed with Carollo Engineers. It examines the resource, technological, financial and contractual issues utilities should consider before approving or supporting data center projects. These include water supply reliability, infrastructure capacity, wastewater impacts, environmental considerations and the recovery of costs associated with development. According to a press release, the report builds on AWWA’s 2025 publication, Cooling the Cloud: Water Utilities in a Data-Driven World, which examined the relationship between data center development, water utilities and local communities. “Water utilities are foundational to local economic development and industrial growth, making their early involvement in community planning essential for major development projects,” said David LaFrance, CEO, AWWA. “Each community will ultimately consider many factors and viewpoints as it assesses data center proposals, AWWA looks forward to working with our many members to share additional insights on data center development and support informed decision-making.” The report outlines a project-by-project approach, urging utilities to first assess data centers’ cooling technologies, projected average and peak water consumption, wastewater needs and potential future expansion. These factors should be weighed against available water supplies, infrastructure capacity, reuse opportunities and environmental impacts before utilities commit resources. It also calls on utilities to establish clear agreements with developers covering infrastructure investments, project costs and each party’s responsibilities as developments evolve. The aim is to prevent existing customers from bearing additional financial burdens. The report further emphasizes early public engagement, with utilities encouraged to disclose projected water demand, system capacity, potential rate impacts and unresolved concerns. Community benefit agreements are also suggested as a way to improve transparency and ensure accountability. It is noteworthy that the AWWA report does not take a position for or against data center development, but is intended to help utilities evaluate proposals based on their individual circumstances.

artigo.texto: KITCHENER, ON, Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Recurrent Energy, a subsidiary of Canadian Solar Inc. ("Canadian Solar") (NASDAQ: CSIQ) and a leading global developer, owner, and operator of solar and energy storage assets, today announced the sale of two standalone BESS projects in France to BW ESS, a global energy storage owner-operator. The portfolio comprises two projects: Baixas, located in the Pyrénées-Orientales department, with a capacity of 100 MW / 400 MWh, and Coquainvilliers, located in Calvados, with a capacity of 100 MW / 400 MWh. Both projects benefit from advanced transmission-level grid connection positions and have been developed around strong grid fundamentals, including very limited expected network constraints. Together, they will provide 200 MW / 800 MWh of flexible capacity to the French electricity system. Recurrent Energy originated and developed both projects, including securing the land, advancing grid connection, and managing permitting and local stakeholder engagement. BW ESS will acquire the projects, marking the first transaction between the two companies and BW ESS' entry into the French energy market. Recurrent Energy will continue to lead the projects through the remaining development phase, drawing on its local market knowledge, technical capabilities, and experience in delivering renewable energy and storage projects. Once the remaining development milestones have been achieved, BW ESS will lead the delivery of the assets through construction and into commercial operation. BW ESS intends to own and operate the assets over the long term. Erik Strømsø, CEO and Co-Founder of BW ESS, commented: "We are excited to work with Recurrent Energy through the next phase and to apply BW ESS' long-term owner-operator expertise as we bring these assets into construction and operation. Entering France is a significant milestone for BW ESS and a natural next step in the expansion of our global energy storage platform. These acquisitions give us an immediate 200 MW / 800 MWh platform in the country and provide a strong foundation for building a sizeable French portfolio. France has a strong nuclear base, but it also has a growing need for flexibility as weather-sensitive demand and an evolving generation mix create more variable system conditions. Batteries can complement France's nuclear backbone by adding the rapid-response flexibility needed to balance the system, absorb surplus power, and make low-carbon generation available when it is most valuable." Dylan Marx, CEO of Recurrent Energy, said: "This transaction with BW ESS showcases our ability to create value through the delivery of high-quality BESS projects, while remaining closely involved in their development through to commercial operation. It is a strong testament to the BESS platform we have built in France and our ability to continue scaling it. Once operational, the projects will provide flexible storage capacity to support grid stability, balance supply and demand, and facilitate the further integration of renewable energy into the French electricity system." artigo.texto: Maryland launches $200 million in grants for solar and battery storage The U.S. state is accepting applications for Megawatts for Maryland, funded with $200 million over two years. Projects will be selected through an auction based on megawatt-hours delivered per dollar. Maryland has begun accepting applications for a grant program aimed at developers of solar, wind and battery storage projects. Named Megawatts for Maryland, the program was established this year by the state's General Assembly, with $200 million over two years drawn from an existing fund. It joins a broader wave of public support, such as the subsidised rooftop solar programme launched in Thailand. The funds target projects that have already completed some steps, including acquiring property and applying to the Maryland Public Service Commission or the regional grid operator. Selection through an auction "We want to make sure that these are real projects," said Kelly Speakes-Backman, director of the Maryland Energy Administration. The agency will distribute the funds through a competitive auction and select the projects delivering the most megawatt-hours per dollar. Projects must come online within seven years of receiving the grant. Together, they are expected to deliver "several hundred megawatts," enough to power about 150,000 homes per year, according to Speakes-Backman. Policymakers hope the added supply will help reduce electricity prices, as in other markets where battery storage is expanding rapidly. "This is not going to be something that impacts our bill tomorrow," she said. Funding drawn from compliance payments The $100 million per year comes from "alternative compliance payments" that electricity suppliers make in lieu of meeting the state's rules on the share of renewables in their portfolios. The payments have grown sharply in recent years, in part because the required share of solar is rising faster than projects are built. They flow into the Strategic Energy Investment Fund. Democratic lawmakers have used the money to balance the state budget, which prompted opposition from the right and from climate groups, and to create additional climate and energy programs. State leaders also hope the grants will partly make up for investment tax credits (ITC) for renewable projects, created under the Inflation Reduction Act and canceled by President Donald Trump's administration. "It's not going to necessarily fully replace the ITC," Speakes-Backman said, adding that she does not see it as a drop in the bucket: "This is a really big deal: $200 million toward in-state generation." Timeline and local acceptance Initial applications from developers are due by Nov. 30. State officials will then confirm eligibility, and qualified developers will have until Jan. 22 to submit a bid. Across the state, solar farms and battery storage facilities have at times provoked strong community pushback. In the first application, developers must show they notified a local elected official. In January, they will provide community engagement and community benefit plans. The law nonetheless requires winners to be chosen purely on megawatts delivered per dollar spent, Speakes-Backman said. Senate President Bill Ferguson said the program, passed in the Utility RELIEF Act, aims to increase supply and help lower utility bills. - Gas44.1 % - Nuclear16.1 % - Coal15.7 % - Solar10.6 % - Wind8.3 % - Hydro3.5 % - Bioenergy0.9 % - Other fossil0.5 % - Other renewables0.4 %
